_about: Hand-checked, per-exchange facts for the CCXT exchange pages. Every entry cites official exchange pages (or a named practitioner source) with the date it was read. Facts that come from CCXT metadata live in ccxt_exchange_facts.json instead. Do not add region or country labels (Rob, 2026-10-23). No 'tested by us' or 'community supported' labels (Rob, 2026-10-23).

aftermath.summary: Aftermath Perpetuals is a fully onchain perpetual futures exchange on the Sui blockchain, run by Aftermath Finance. Every order, cancel, trade and liquidation runs onchain, and positions use USDC as collateral.
signup_steps: There is no account form. Open aftermath.finance, click Login / Connect, and connect a Sui wallet (Aftermath suggests Sui Wallet, Nightly or Phantom), or log in with zkLogin.
Hold a little SUI for gas and native USDC on Sui for collateral.
Create a Perpetuals account and deposit USDC into it. One wallet can own several Perpetuals accounts (sub-accounts).
api_key_steps: Aftermath has no API key and secret. Transactions are signed with a Sui wallet's private key. Aftermath says to always use an agent wallet for automation, never your main (admin) wallet.
Create a new Sui wallet just for the bot and save its address and private key.
With your main wallet connected, open the Agent Wallets page (https://aftermath.finance/automation) and authorize the bot wallet as an agent on your Perpetuals account.
Give the bot wallet a small amount of SUI for gas, or set up a GasPool from your main wallet to pay its gas.
Give LumiBot the bot wallet's address as ``walletAddress`` and its private key as ``privateKey``.
aftermath.permissions: There are no permission boxes to set. Aftermath says an agent wallet can do everything except withdraw collateral, grant or revoke other agent wallets, and revoke builder code approvals. So the agent wallet can trade but cannot withdraw. The admin wallet can revoke it at any time.
aftermath.testnet_note: CCXT points the sandbox at Aftermath's testnet API on https://testnet.aftermath.finance. Set ``AFTERMATH_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Aftermath's docs do not include a testnet guide, so check the testnet site for how to get test funds.
extra_notes: CCXT symbols for Aftermath look like ``BTC/USD:USDC`` (priced in USD, settled in USDC). There are no spot markets in CCXT for Aftermath.
Trading needs a Perpetuals account. CCXT's position and open order calls ask for an ``accountNumber``, which ``fetch_accounts`` returns for the wallet.
An account can have up to 10 active agent wallets at once. Use one agent wallet per bot so you can revoke one without stopping the others.
Collateral must be allocated from the account to a market before it can back a position. Liquidation on one sub-account does not affect your other sub-accounts.

alpaca.summary: Alpaca is a trading platform with an API for stocks and crypto. Its crypto API lets you trade coins such as BTC around the clock against USD, USDT and USDC.
signup_steps: Sign up for an Alpaca Trading API account with your email address.
To trade real money, open a live account and finish Alpaca's account application. Anyone can start with a paper-only account.
Your account comes with a paper trading account. Alpaca starts it with a $100,000 simulated balance.
api_key_steps: Log in to the Alpaca dashboard.
Pick the account you want the bot to use: paper or live. Each one has its own keys.
On the Home page, generate your API Key and Secret Key.
Copy the Secret Key right away. Alpaca shows it only once.
If you make a new paper account later, generate new keys for it.
alpaca.permissions: Alpaca's docs describe one key ID and one secret key per account, with no separate permission boxes. Anyone with the key can trade the account, so keep it private. If Alpaca ever shows a withdrawal or transfer option for a key, leave it off.
alpaca.testnet_note: Alpaca's sandbox is its paper trading account at https://paper-api.alpaca.markets. It fills orders against real-time quotes but sends nothing to a live market, and it uses separate paper keys. Set ``ALPACA_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: ``alpaca`` is also the name of LumiBot's own Alpaca broker, which keeps priority. To reach Alpaca's crypto API through CCXT, set ``TRADING_BROKER=ccxt:alpaca``.
Paper keys and live keys are different. Alpaca says live keys do not work with the paper API, and paper keys do not work with the live API.
Alpaca crypto pairs use a slash, for example ``BTC/USD``. Alpaca supports market, limit and stop limit orders for crypto, with ``gtc`` and ``ioc`` time in force.
sources: Alpaca Learn: How to get Alpaca Trading API key and start connection

apex.summary: ApeX Omni is a decentralized exchange (DEX) for perpetual futures that you use with a crypto wallet. It supports deposits and withdrawals on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Mantle and Arbitrum.
signup_steps: Open ApeX Omni and connect your crypto wallet. Your wallet is your account, and you sign a message with it to set up access.
Deposit funds into your Omni funding account, then move them to your Perps account to trade.
For practice, use the ApeX Omni testnet at https://testnet.omni.apex.exchange. It runs on test chains, and you can get free test assets from its faucet at https://testnet.omni.apex.exchange/faucet.
api_key_steps: Connect your wallet and open the key management page at https://omni.apex.exchange/keyManagement.
Click Generate API and confirm with a wallet signature. Choose a passphrase you will remember: ApeX cannot recover it, and if you lose it you must make a new key.
Save the three values ApeX shows: the API key, the secret key and your passphrase.
On the same page, click Omni Key to get your seeds. ApeX needs these to sign every order, on top of the API key.
Store all four values somewhere safe. Each account can have up to 30 API keys.
apex.permissions: ApeX Omni works differently from a normal exchange. The API key, secret and passphrase let your bot read the account, but orders, transfers and withdrawals also need a second signature made with your Omni Key seeds. That means anyone with your API key and seeds together could also move money, so treat the seeds like a wallet private key: keep them only on the machine that runs your bot and never share them. Never give LumiBot your main wallet's private key; the Omni Key seeds are all it needs.
apex.testnet_note: ApeX Omni runs a full testnet at https://testnet.omni.apex.exchange, with a faucet for test assets. Make separate keys and an Omni Key on the testnet site. Set ``APEX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: ApeX Omni needs three API values (API key, secret and passphrase) plus your Omni Key seeds. In CCXT terms, the passphrase is ``password`` and the seeds go in the exchange options, for example ``"options": {"seeds": "..."}`` in a code config. Without the seeds, CCXT can read your account but cannot place orders.
ApeX Omni markets are perpetual futures, so use the full CCXT symbol such as ``BTC/USDT:USDT``. ApeX's own API writes it as ``BTC-USDT``.
ApeX says to trade you deposit into your Omni funding account and then transfer funds to your Perps account. Make that transfer before starting your bot.
sources: ApeX Omni API docs: introduction, testnet and signatures
ApeX Omni API docs: Best Practice (API key credentials and Omni Key)

backpack.summary: Backpack is a crypto exchange and wallet. It offers spot trading and perpetual futures in one margin system, plus lending, borrowing and sub-accounts.
signup_steps: Create a Backpack account with your email, or sign up with Google or Apple where Backpack offers it.
Finish identity verification (KYC). Backpack says most checks take a few minutes to a few hours, and a manual review can take 1 to 3 days.
Turn on two-factor authentication. Backpack has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to Backpack on the website. Backpack only lets you create API keys on the web, not in the app.
Go to Settings, then API Keys (https://backpack.exchange/settings/api-keys), and click New API Key.
Enter a name for the key and choose the sub-account the bot should trade in.
Leave the Public Key field blank. Backpack recommends this for most people.
Do not press the Read Only button, because a read-only key cannot place orders. Click Create.
Save the API key and API secret somewhere safe right away.
backpack.permissions: A normal Backpack key can read your account and trade. The Read Only button limits a key to view-only access, so leave it off for a trading bot. Leave withdrawals off: Backpack says API withdrawals need extra security setup with two-factor authentication, and a bot never needs to move money out of your account.
backpack.testnet_note: Backpack has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BACKPACK_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Backpack markets are priced in USDC, so use ``USDC`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/USDC``). Perpetuals use the CCXT form ``BTC/USDC:USDC``. Backpack's own API writes these as ``BTC_USDC`` and ``BTC_USDC_PERP``; CCXT converts them for you.
Each API key belongs to one sub-account. Backpack sub-accounts each have their own margin, positions and risk settings, so a separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
Backpack applies rate limits per sub-account: about 2,000 requests per minute on normal REST endpoints, and 30 per minute on historical data such as candles. Too many requests return HTTP 429.
Backpack signs API requests with an ED25519 key pair, so its keys look different from most exchanges. Copy the API key and API secret exactly as Backpack shows them.
sources: Backpack Help Center: Generate API keys for Backpack Exchange
Backpack Help Center: create a new account FAQs

bequant.summary: Bequant Global is a crypto exchange built for professional traders. It offers spot trading, margin trading and perpetual futures, with access through FIX, WebSocket and REST APIs.
signup_steps: Click Register on the Bequant home page, choose a username and password, then add your legal name and phone number and click Finish Registration.
Confirm your email address with the link Bequant sends you, then finish account verification.
Turn on two-factor authentication under Settings, then the Security tab.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the API settings page.
Click New API key. Bequant creates a public API key and a secret key with no access rights yet.
Copy the secret key right away. Bequant hides it once you leave the page, and a lost secret means you must make a new key.
Tick the access rights the bot needs (see below). Bequant asks you to confirm by email and 2FA code when you add order rights.
Use the ON/OFF switch to turn a key off when you are not using it, or the trash icon to delete it.
bequant.permissions: Turn on Order book, History, Trading balance (to read your balance and orders) and Place/cancel orders (to trade). Leave Withdraw cryptocurrencies off, and do not use Allow all. Bequant warns that actions sent through the API need no 2FA code or email check, so the key alone is enough to act.
bequant.testnet_note: Bequant's own API docs and help center describe no sandbox or demo site. CCXT's test URL for Bequant points to a HitBTC demo server, not a Bequant site, so do not rely on it. Test with a very small amount, leave ``BEQUANT_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bequant keeps a separate wallet balance and spot (trading) balance. Move funds to your spot balance before the bot trades. The Payment information right is only needed if your code moves funds between them.
A verified account can create sub-accounts from the Sub-Accounts tab, and each sub-account has its own API keys. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
Bequant lists markets in many quotes, including USDT, USD, EUR and GBP. In LumiBot use the CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT``.

Bequant Help Center: How to open account on Bequant Global?
Bequant Help Center: How to protect your account from intruders
Bequant Help Center: How to create Sub-Account?

bigone.summary: BigONE is a crypto exchange with spot trading, leverage and futures. Its contract API covers USDT-margined and coin-margined contracts.
signup_steps: Sign up on the BigONE website or app with an email address or phone number, and enter the code BigONE sends within 15 minutes.
Set a password and agree to the User Agreement and Privacy Statement.
Turn on two-factor authentication (email or Google Authenticator), which BigONE asks for when you create an API key. Complete KYC too; BigONE's Help Center has a KYC guide.
api_key_steps: Log in to your BigONE account and go to API Settings (also listed as User Center, API Management).
Click Create API Key.
Choose the permission scopes (see below) and add your bot's IP address to the IP whitelist.
Finish the two-factor authentication (2FA) check.
Save the API Secret right away. BigONE shows it only once. If you lose it, delete the key and make a new one.
bigone.permissions: Turn on View Account Balance Information, View Order Information, Create Orders and View Trade Information. For contracts, also turn on Access Contract and Create Contract. Leave Execute Withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bigone.testnet_note: BigONE has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``BIGONE_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: BigONE needs only two credentials: the API key (``BIGONE_API_KEY``) and the API Secret (``BIGONE_API_SECRET``). There is no passphrase.
Each key can be bound to up to 20 IP addresses or ranges (CIDR like ``192.168.1.0/24`` works). BigONE recommends always using the IP whitelist.
A 10403 Permission denied error means the key is missing a scope or the request came from an IP that is not on the whitelist. You can edit scopes and IPs later, but you cannot see the secret again.
Spot symbols look like ``BTC/USDT``. USDT-margined contracts use the CCXT form ``BTC/USDT:USDT``, and coin-margined ones ``BTC/USD:BTC``.
sources: BigONE API docs: API Key Setup
BigONE API docs: Contract Trading Introduction
BigONE Help Center: How to Register BigONE Account (APP)

binance.summary: Binance is one of the largest crypto exchanges. It offers spot trading, margin, futures and more, with hundreds of coins to trade.
signup_steps: Create a Binance account on the website or app.
Finish identity verification and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Binance requires both before you can make an API key, and also a first deposit of any amount to your Spot Wallet.
For practice, log in to the Binance Spot Test Network at https://testnet.binance.vision and make a separate test API key there. Test funds are not real and test keys only work on the test network.
api_key_steps: Log in and go to Profile, then API Management (https://www.binance.com/en/usercenter/settings/api-management).
Click Create API.
Pick System-generated (you get an API key and a Secret Key). Self-generated keys use Ed25519 or RSA and need your own key pair.
Enter a label for the key, then confirm with your 2FA device or passkey.
Click Edit restrictions, add your bot's IP address, and turn on the trading permission (see below).
Copy the API key and Secret Key and store them safely.
binance.permissions: Turn on Enable Reading and Enable Spot & Margin Trading. Leave Enable Withdrawals off. Binance only lets a system-generated key trade if you add an IP address restriction. Without an IP list the key can only read.
binance.testnet_note: Binance runs a Spot Test Network at https://testnet.binance.vision with its own keys and free test funds. It is reset about once a month. Set ``BINANCE_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: Always add an IP whitelist. Binance says a key with no IP list keeps only read access, and trading permission without an IP list used to expire after 30 days.
A key made before you opened your Futures account cannot get Futures permission. Open Futures first, then create the key, if you plan to trade futures.

CCXT uses separate ids for some Binance products: ``binanceusdm`` for USDT-margined futures, ``binancecoinm`` for coin-margined futures and ``binanceus`` for the separate Binance.US exchange. Use ``binance`` for spot.
The Spot Test Network only has the ``/api`` endpoints, not ``/sapi``, so wallet and sub-account calls do not work there.
sources: Binance Support: How to Create API Keys on Binance?
Binance Support: Updates to API Key Permission Rules
Binance Developer Docs: Margin trading best practice
Binance Academy: Binance AI Agent Skills (Edit Restrictions and Enable Spot & Margin Trading)

binancecoinm.summary: Binance COIN-M is the coin-margined futures side of Binance. Contracts are priced in USD but margined and settled in the coin itself (for example BTC), and Binance offers both perpetual and dated delivery contracts.
signup_steps: Create a Binance account and finish identity verification.
Turn on two-factor authentication and make a deposit of any amount to your Spot Wallet. Binance requires all three before you can create an API key.
Open your Futures account before you create the API key. A key made before the Futures account exists cannot get the Futures permission.
api_key_steps: Log in, click the profile icon and choose Account.
Go to API Management and click Create API.
Choose System-generated (you get an API key and a Secret Key). Self-generated Ed25519 or RSA keys are the other option.
Enter a label for the key and confirm with your two-factor devices or passkey.
Edit the key restrictions: limit access to the IP address of your bot, then turn on the permissions below. Save the Secret Key right away.
binancecoinm.permissions: Turn on Enable Reading and the Futures permission. Binance only allows permissions beyond reading when the key is limited to trusted IP addresses (or uses a self-generated key), so add your bot's IP first. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
binancecoinm.testnet_note: Binance runs Futures Demo Trading at https://demo.binance.com with its own Demo Trading API keys. Binance says the futures testnet is only available through the API. Set ``BINANCECOINM_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: COIN-M symbols use the full CCXT form ``BTC/USD:BTC`` for the perpetual. Dated contracts add the expiry, for example ``BTC/USD:BTC-261225``.
One BTC COIN-M contract is worth 100 USD, so the smallest order is one contract (about 100 USD), not 50. Your margin is held in BTC, so its dollar value moves with the BTC price.
Binance has three CCXT ids: ``binance`` for spot, ``binanceusdm`` for USDT-margined futures and ``binancecoinm`` for coin-margined futures. Pick ``binancecoinm`` for this page.
If you use Portfolio Margin, Binance says the API key cannot get the Futures permission.
sources: Binance FAQ: How to Create API Keys on Binance?
Binance Developer Docs: COIN-M futures general info
Binance Developer Docs: Derivatives quick start (Futures Testnet and Demo Trading)

binanceus.summary: Binance.US is a crypto exchange for buying, selling and trading more than 200 cryptocurrencies. It offers spot trading with advanced trading tools, plus convert, OTC and staking.
signup_steps: Create a Binance.US account with your email and a password (Google Sign-In also works), then enter the code Binance.US emails you.
Turn on SMS two-factor authentication. Binance.US requires it to finish sign-up; you can switch to an authenticator app later.
Complete Basic Verification. Binance.US says you must finish it before you can open API Management.
api_key_steps: Log in to Binance.US in a web browser.
Hover over your email or profile icon in the top menu and choose API Management (https://www.binance.us/settings/api-management).
Pick the Exchange API key type and enter a clear label so you can find the key later.
Click Create and finish two-factor authentication. Binance.US may ask for both your 2FA code and an email confirmation.
Copy the API key and secret right away. Binance.US shows the secret only once.
Click Edit restrictions to set permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address.
binanceus.permissions: New keys start with Enable Reading only. Also turn on Enable Spot Trading so your bot can place orders. Leave Enable Withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
binanceus.testnet_note: Binance.US has no sandbox. Its API docs do not offer a test site, and the test URLs CCXT lists for this id belong to the separate Binance testnet, where Binance.US keys do not work. Test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BINANCEUS_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Add an IP restriction to your key. Binance.US resets keys to read-only if they go unused for 90 days and have no IP whitelist.
Binance.US is a different exchange from Binance. Use the CCXT id ``binanceus`` with Binance.US keys, not ``binance``.
Binance.US also lists BTC against USDT and USDC, so you can use ``BTC/USDT`` or ``BTC/USDC`` if your cash is held in a stablecoin.
Binance.US recommends deleting old keys and making new ones about every 90 days, and deleting keys you no longer use.
sources: Binance.US Help Center: How to create an API key on Binance.US
Binance.US Help Center: API keys best practices and safety tips
Binance.US Help Center: How to create your account and pass identity verification

binanceusdm.summary: Binance USDⓈ-M Futures are the Binance futures contracts that are quoted and settled in USDT or USDC. They come as perpetual and quarterly contracts.
signup_steps: Create a Binance account, finish identity verification and turn on two-factor authentication (2FA).
Make a deposit of any amount to your Spot Wallet. Binance asks for this to activate the account before you can create API keys.
Open a USDⓈ-M Futures account before you make the API key. A key made before your Futures account was turned on cannot get the Futures permission later.
api_key_steps: Log in, click your profile icon and choose Account, then open API Management.
Click Create API.
Choose System-generated (you get an API key and a Secret Key). Self-generated keys (Ed25519 or RSA) also work if you make your own key pair.
Enter a label for the key and confirm with your 2FA device or passkey.
Click Edit restrictions, add the IP address of the machine that runs your bot, then turn on the permissions below and save.
Copy the API key and Secret Key and keep them somewhere safe.
binanceusdm.permissions: Turn on Enable Reading and Enable Futures. Leave Enable Withdrawals off, a trading bot never needs it. Binance only lets a system-generated key do more than read when you add an IP access restriction, so add your bot's IP address first.
binanceusdm.testnet_note: Binance has a free test area for futures. Binance's help page now points to Futures Demo Trading at https://demo.binance.com/en/futures, where you make separate test API keys under API Management. CCXT's sandbox mode for binanceusdm uses Binance's futures testnet address (https://testnet.binancefuture.com). Make sure your test keys come from the test site that LumiBot connects to. Set ``BINANCEUSDM_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: ``binanceusdm`` covers only USDⓈ-M futures. Use the CCXT id ``binance`` for spot trading and ``binancecoinm`` for COIN-M futures (settled in the coin itself).
Symbols use the full CCXT form: ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the USDT perpetual and ``BTC/USDC:USDC`` for the USDC perpetual.

If the Futures box is missing or greyed out on your key, your Futures account was probably opened after the key was made, or Portfolio Margin is on. Binance says such keys cannot get the Futures permission, so make a new key.
sources: Binance FAQ: How to Create API Keys on Binance?
Binance FAQ: How to Test Functions on Binance Spot Testnet and Futures Demo Trading?
Binance FAQ: What Are USDⓈ-Margined Futures and COIN-Margined Futures?
Binance Developer Docs: USDⓈ-M Futures General Info

bingx.summary: BingX is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading, perpetual futures (USDT, USDC and coin margined), copy trading and trading bots. BingX's API covers spot and perpetual futures.
signup_steps: Sign up on bingx.com or in the BingX app with an email address or phone number.
Finish identity verification: open your profile icon, then Identity Verification, and upload photos of an ID document plus a selfie holding it. BingX says advanced verification takes 2 to 10 minutes.
Set up two-factor authentication (Google Authenticator or SMS). You need it to create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in on the website, open your profile icon and go to API Management (https://bingx.com/en/accounts/api).
Click Create API and give the key a clear name, for example the name of your bot.
Choose the permissions (see below).
Add your bot's IP address. One key can hold up to 20 IP addresses, separated by commas.
Finish the 2FA check, then copy the API Key and Secret Key. BingX shows the secret only once.
bingx.permissions: Turn on Read plus Spot Trading, or Perpetual Futures Trading if your bot trades perpetuals. Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bingx.testnet_note: BingX has no separate testnet site. CCXT's sandbox uses BingX's demo trading API at https://open-api-vst.bingx.com, which trades with VST (virtual USDT) in the demo trading account and works for perpetual futures. Set ``BINGX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Demo trading does not cover spot, so test spot with a very small real amount.
extra_notes: Bind your key to an IP address. BingX deletes keys that have trading, transfer or sub-account permissions, no IP address and no API calls for 14 days in a row. Keys with an IP address, or read-only keys, do not expire.
Each main account and each sub-account can keep up to 20 active API keys. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
BingX's API only covers Spot and Perpetual Futures. Standard Futures and copy trading are not reachable through it.
BingX writes symbols like ``BTC-USDT``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/USDT`` for spot and ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the USDT perpetual.

bit2c.summary: Bit2C is a crypto exchange. You trade coins such as Bitcoin and Ethereum against the shekel.
signup_steps: Register with your mobile phone number, then choose a username, a strong password and your email address.
Confirm your email with the link Bit2C sends, then confirm your phone with the link in the SMS.
Finish identity verification (KYC) and upload the documents Bit2C asks for before you trade.
api_key_steps: Log in to your Bit2C account.
Go to the API keys screen in your account settings.
Create a new API key. You can also edit or delete keys there.
Enter the code Bit2C sends you by SMS. Bit2C asks for this code every time you create, edit or delete a key.
Save the public key and the secret key somewhere safe.
bit2c.permissions: Bit2C's own pages do not list the permission names. Give the key what it needs to read your balance and orders and to trade. If the key screen offers withdrawals, leave them off.
bit2c.testnet_note: Bit2C has no sandbox, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BIT2C_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bit2C prices are in shekels, and CCXT names the pair ``BTC/NIS``.
Bit2C uses two-step checks with a code sent by SMS. You need it to log in, to send crypto out, and to manage API keys, so keep your phone number current.
Every private request carries a nonce that must go up each time. Run only one bot per key so two programs do not fight over the nonce.
sources: Bit2C FAQ: registration and two-step verification
Bit2C guide: protecting your account with SMS two-step verification

bitbank.summary: bitbank is a crypto exchange with prices in Japanese yen. Its API lets you read prices and charts, place and check orders, and read your trade history.
signup_steps: Create a bitbank account and finish the identity verification bitbank asks for.
Set up a passkey or two-step authentication. bitbank asks for one of these when you create or view an API key.
bitbank has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to bitbank and choose API from the menu.
Press the APIキーの発行 (Issue API key) button.
Type a label so you can tell what the key is for, then choose the permissions (see below).
Press 確認する (Confirm), check the details and press 発行する (Issue).
Finish the extra check with your passkey (or a two-step or SMS code if you have no passkey).
To see the key, press the arrow next to it in the API menu and pass the security check. The screen shows the API key and the secret key.
bitbank.permissions: Turn on the view permission (参照) and the trading permission so your bot can read balances and orders and place trades. Leave the withdrawal permission off. bitbank warns that anyone who has your API key can place orders and request withdrawals.
bitbank.testnet_note: bitbank has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITBANK_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: bitbank markets are priced in Japanese yen, so use ``JPY`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/JPY``). bitbank's own API writes pairs like ``btc_jpy``; LumiBot and CCXT use the ``BTC/JPY`` form.
bitbank's official API docs live on GitHub at https://github.com/bitbankinc/bitbank-api-docs, with a Japanese version. The help center points there.
If you delete a key in the API menu, it stops working right away, so a bot using it can no longer trade.
sources: bitbank Support: APIキーの発行とAPI仕様の確認方法 (how to issue an API key)
bitbank Support: APIについて (about the API)

bitfinex.summary: Bitfinex is a digital asset trading platform for traders and liquidity providers. It offers spot (exchange) trading, margin trading, margin funding and derivatives.
signup_steps: On https://www.bitfinex.com/ click Sign Up, then enter a username, email and password. Confirm your email with the 6-digit code or the link Bitfinex sends you.
Turn on two-factor authentication. Bitfinex will not let you use its features until 2FA is set up.
Finish account verification. Bitfinex has no separate testnet, but you can create a Paper Trading sub-account for practice (see below).
api_key_steps: Log in on the Bitfinex website and open the API Key page (https://www.bitfinex.com/api).
Choose the Create New Key tab.
Pick the permissions (see below). Under IP Access restrictions you can whitelist up to 20 IP addresses, such as the machine that runs your bot.
Give the key a label and click Generate API Key. Confirm with your 2FA code or security key.
Open the confirmation email and click Create API Key. Use the same browser you use for Bitfinex.
Copy the API Key and API Key Secret right away. Bitfinex shows them only once.
bitfinex.permissions: Turn on read access for Account Info, Account History, Orders and Wallets, and turn on write access for Orders so the bot can create and cancel orders. Add Margin Trading only if your bot trades margin or derivatives. Leave Withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account. Make the key on the website: Bitfinex says logins and keys made through the mobile app start with every permission on.
bitfinex.testnet_note: Bitfinex has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITFINEX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``. For practice, Bitfinex lets you create a Paper Trading sub-account with test balances; keys for it are made while you are switched into that sub-account.
extra_notes: Bitfinex lists BTC against USD, USDT, EUR, GBP and others. Spot is plain ``BTC/USD``. Perpetuals use the CCXT form ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.

A Paper Trading sub-account is created from Sub-Accounts, Create new sub-account, Paper. It needs its own email and username, and it can never be turned into a regular account. Its test tokens have no value.
Bitfinex sub-accounts share the master account's trading volume and fee tier, and the master account can restrict sub-account withdrawals. A master account can have up to 100 sub-accounts.

Bitfinex REST limits range from 10 to 90 requests per minute depending on the endpoint, and going over blocks your IP for 60 seconds. Use a separate API key for each bot, because each key keeps its own nonce sequence.
sources: Bitfinex Support: How to create and revoke a Bitfinex API Key
Bitfinex Support: How to create an account on Bitfinex
Bitfinex Support: Paper Trading at Bitfinex
Bitfinex API docs: requirements and limitations

bitflyer.summary: bitFlyer is a bitcoin and crypto exchange. Its bitFlyer Lightning trading platform offers spot trading and a bitcoin CFD product (Crypto CFD), with a public and private HTTP API.
signup_steps: Create a bitFlyer account on the official site.
Finish account verification. bitFlyer says you must sign up and verify your account to use its APIs and bitFlyer Lightning.
Turn on two-factor authentication. bitFlyer highly recommends it.
api_key_steps: Log in to bitFlyer Lightning at https://lightning.bitflyer.com.
Open the developer page (https://lightning.bitflyer.com/developer), where bitFlyer issues API keys.
Generate a new API key and set its permissions. bitFlyer lets you pick permissions for each key.
Save the API key and API secret somewhere safe. bitFlyer says never to store the secret in plain text, in your program or in Git.
Optional: the private endpoint GET /v1/me/getpermissions lists what your key is allowed to do, so you can check it.
bitflyer.permissions: Give the key the permissions to read your balance, orders and executions, and to place and cancel orders. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bitflyer.testnet_note: bitFlyer has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it. The bitFlyer Lightning API Playground is a live environment that uses real funds, so it is not a test site. Test with a very small amount, leave ``BITFLYER_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: bitFlyer product codes look like ``BTC_JPY``. In LumiBot use the CCXT form, for example ``BTC/JPY``. CCXT also lists ``BTC/USD`` and ``BTC/EUR``; use the market your bitFlyer account can trade.
The bitcoin CFD product uses the product code ``FX_BTC_JPY`` on bitFlyer. In CCXT it shows up as ``BTC/JPY:JPY``.
bitFlyer limits private API calls to 500 per 5 minutes, and some order calls to 300 per 5 minutes in total. Going over blocks requests for a while, so avoid very short bot loops.
bitFlyer only needs an API key and secret. There is no passphrase.
sources: bitFlyer Europe blog: Bitcoin trading bot using bitFlyer Lightning APIs

bitget.summary: Bitget is a large crypto exchange with spot trading, margin, USDT and coin margined futures, and copy trading. Its newer Unified Trading Account keeps spot and futures in one account.
signup_steps: Create a Bitget account on the website.
Open Identity Verification from the profile icon and finish identity verification (KYC).
Turn on two-factor authentication. Bitget asks for email, SMS and Google verification codes when you create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in on the Bitget website and open API Key Management (https://www.bitget.com/account/newapi). You can also reach it from your profile icon, then API.
Click Create API.
Add a note (a name) and type a passphrase. Write the passphrase down: Bitget cannot show it again, and you cannot change it later.
Set the permissions (see below) and bind the IP address of the machine that runs your bot.
Enter your email, SMS and Google verification codes.
Copy the API key and secret key and store them with the passphrase.
bitget.permissions: Give the key read and write access for trading (Bitget calls this trade, read and write) so the bot can place and cancel orders. Read-only access to account information is enough for balances. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bitget.testnet_note: Bitget has no testnet in CCXT, so leave ``BITGET_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``. Bitget does have a demo trading mode with its own Demo API Keys (switch to Demo mode, then API Key Management), but LumiBot's sandbox setting does not point there. Test with a very small amount instead.
extra_notes: Bitget needs three credentials: the API key, the secret key and your passphrase. Put the passphrase in ``BITGET_API_PASSPHRASE`` (``"password"`` in a code config). If you lose the passphrase you must delete the key and make a new one.
Bitget strongly recommends binding an IP address to every API key. Each account can create up to 50 API keys.
Sub-accounts can create their own API keys once the main account turns on API Key Management for that sub-account. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
Spot symbols look like ``BTC/USDT``. USDT perpetuals use the full CCXT form ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
sources: Bitget Support Center: API Creation Guide
Bitget API docs: Quick Start (API keys, permissions, passphrase, demo trading)

bithumb.summary: Bithumb is a crypto exchange where you buy and sell coins against the Korean won (KRW), for example the KRW-BTC market. Its API lets you check prices and balances and place buy and sell orders automatically.
signup_steps: Create a Bithumb account on the website or app.
Finish identity verification (customer verification). Bithumb says trading, including API trading, can be blocked until you do.
Bithumb has no testnet, so plan to start with a very small trade.
api_key_steps: Log in on a computer, click your name at the top, then Account Management (계정관리), then API Management (API 관리).
Choose the API functions the key may use (API 활성 항목). See the permissions below.
Enter the IP address of the machine that runs your bot. You can enter up to 5 addresses, and the key is limited if you leave this empty.
Agree to the terms and click Create API Key (API Key 생성), then finish the ownership check.
Copy the Secret Key right away. Bithumb shows it only once.
bithumb.permissions: Turn on asset lookup (자산조회), order lookup (주문조회) and placing orders (주문하기). Leave withdrawals (출금하기) off. Bithumb warns that an API key can withdraw without any extra check, so never give a bot that function. To change functions later you must delete the key and make a new one.
bithumb.testnet_note: Bithumb has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``BITHUMB_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bithumb keys last one year and cannot be extended. When a key expires, delete it and create a new one. Each account can hold up to 10 keys, counting expired ones.
Bithumb now issues both API 1.0 and API 2.0 keys. CCXT's ``bithumb`` exchange calls the older API 1.0 endpoints (such as ``info/balance``), so make an API 1.0 key if Bithumb asks you to choose.
Bithumb writes markets as ``KRW-BTC`` (quote first). In LumiBot and CCXT the same market is ``BTC/KRW``.
Bithumb's help center and API docs are in Korean. The menu names above are given in Korean so you can find them.

bitmart.summary: BitMart is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading, margin trading and futures (USDⓈ-M and COIN-M contracts). It also has a REST API and WebSocket feeds for automated trading.
signup_steps: Create a BitMart account at https://www.bitmart.com/register/en.
Finish identity verification (KYC). BitMart says full access to spot and futures trading needs the KYC 2 level.
Turn on two-factor authentication under Security (phone and Google Authenticator).
api_key_steps: Log in on the BitMart website and click the Account tab.
Open API Management (https://www.bitmart.com/en-US/api-config).
Enter a Memo. This is any text you choose, and BitMart uses it when it checks each request.
Add your bot's IP address (optional, but BitMart recommends it) and pick the permissions below.
Create the key. BitMart shows the Secret Key only once, so copy and save it, then click Confirm.
bitmart.permissions: New BitMart keys start as Read-Only. Add Spot-Trade for spot trading (and Future-Trade if your bot trades futures). Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bitmart.testnet_note: CCXT lists no test URL for BitMart, so LumiBot cannot use a BitMart sandbox. Test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITMART_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: BitMart needs three values: the API key (Access Key), the Secret Key and the Memo. Put the Memo in ``BITMART_UID`` (CCXT's ``uid`` field). BitMart's own FAQ says the ccxt ``uid`` must be the API memo, not your BitMart user ID. A wrong memo gives the error ``Header X-BM-SIGN is wrong``.
If you set an IP whitelist, BitMart rejects requests from any other IP that use that key.
If a key leaks, BitMart says to delete it right away and create a new one. A lost Secret Key cannot be shown again, so you would need a new key.
Sub-account API endpoints need Institution Verification. Sub-account keys also start as Read-only.

bitopro.summary: BitoPro is a crypto exchange for spot trading in BTC, ETH, USDT and other coins. It supports deposits in New Taiwan dollars (TWD).
signup_steps: Register a BitoPro account and finish identity verification. BitoPro asks for this before you can use the API.
Turn on two-factor authentication with Google Authenticator (Account, Security, 2FA). BitoPro suggests using it for both login and withdrawals.
BitoPro has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on the BitoPro website, click your username or avatar in the top right corner and choose API.
On the API Management page, click Create new API key.
Enter a name for the key and choose its permissions (see below), then submit.
Open the confirmation email BitoPro sends to your account email and click the confirm button to turn the key on.
Copy the API key and secret right away. BitoPro shows the secret only once and cannot show it again. If you lose it, delete the key and make a new one.
bitopro.permissions: Give the key permission to read account information and to trade. Leave withdrawals off. A trading bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bitopro.testnet_note: BitoPro has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITOPRO_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Add an IP whitelist to your key. BitoPro says keys with an IP whitelist never expire, while keys without one expire 365 days after they are made (BitoPro emails you 30 days and 7 days before). After that, requests fail with HTTP 401.
BitoPro markets are quoted in TWD or USDT, for example ``BTC/TWD`` or ``BTC/USDT``.
BitoPro deleted API keys made before 2026-05-27 during a July 2026 login update. If your bot uses an older key, check API Management and make a new key.

bitrue.summary: Bitrue is a crypto exchange for spot trading plus USDT-margined and coin-margined futures. Its API covers spot trading, futures trading, asset transfers and market data.
signup_steps: Register an account on bitrue.com.
Finish KYC: click Verification, then ID Verification. Level 1 asks for personal details and your mobile number. Level 2 asks for an ID document and its number.
Bind Google Authenticator under Account Security and back up the security key. Bitrue needs it to create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in and click the API menu under your avatar in the top bar (https://www.bitrue.com/account/api).
Create a new API key and enter a note name for it, for example the name of your bot.
Enter the code from your Google Authenticator app.
Open the link in the email Bitrue sends you to finish verification, then select the permissions you need.
Add your bot's IP address (up to 16 per key, separated by commas).
Copy the secret key right away. Bitrue shows it only once, when the key is created.
bitrue.permissions: Pick read and trading access only. Bitrue's help guide shows the permission choices on screen but does not name them in text, so choose the trading permission for the market you trade (spot or futures). Leave withdrawals off. Bitrue's API docs say a withdraw permission also needs an IP limit and a withdraw address whitelist, so a bot key without it is safer.
bitrue.testnet_note: Bitrue has no sandbox or testnet. Test with a very small amount on your real account, leave ``BITRUE_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bitrue's spot REST API lives at https://openapi.bitrue.com. Bitrue writes symbols with no separator (``BTCUSDT``); in LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/USDT`` for spot and ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the USDT-margined perpetual.
Keep polling modest. Bitrue's docs list order limits of 100 weight per 60 seconds and warn that repeated 429 errors lead to an automatic IP ban lasting from 2 minutes to 3 days.
API keys and secrets are case sensitive. Copy them exactly.
sources: Bitrue Support: Using Bitrue's API Functions
Bitrue Support: How to Start the KYC Verification Process
Bitrue Blog: How to use Bitrue's API function for automatic trading

bitso.summary: Bitso is a crypto exchange for buying, selling and trading digital and fiat currencies. Its order books include BTC against MXN, USD, USDT, BRL and ARS.
signup_steps: Create a Bitso account and finish identity verification.
Turn on two-step verification with an authenticator app. Bitso will not let you create API keys without it.
For practice, also create a separate account on Bitso's testing site at https://stage.bitso.com. Testing keys only work there.
api_key_steps: Log in from the web, not the app. Bitso only lets you make keys on the web.
Click your profile icon, choose API in the left menu, and click Add new API.
Read the security message, check the box and continue.
Name the key. If you like, add up to five IP addresses that may use it.
Choose the permissions (see below) and enter your two-step code.
Save the key and secret right away. Bitso shows them only once.
bitso.permissions: Turn on Buy/sell orders and Balance inquiry. Bitso's API docs call these Place orders and View balances. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bitso.testnet_note: Bitso has a separate testing environment at https://stage.bitso.com with its own accounts and keys. Bitso says to test there, not in production. Set ``BITSO_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: You can have up to six active API keys. If you hit the limit, delete a key you no longer use.
Testing and production accounts are separate. Make keys in each one and use the right keys for each environment.
If you lose the secret, you cannot see it again. Delete that key and create a new one.
sources: Bitso Help Center: Create an API key on Bitso
Bitso API docs: Generate your API credentials
Bitso API docs: Set up your testing environment

bittrade.summary: BitTrade is a registered crypto exchange run by BitTrade Co., Ltd., with prices in Japanese yen. It offers an order-book exchange, a simple buy and sell desk, and leverage trading; its API supports the exchange and the desk but not leverage trading yet.
signup_steps: Open the account form on the BitTrade site or app, enter your email and a password, and confirm the code BitTrade emails you.
Finish identity verification (本人確認) and wait for BitTrade to approve your account.
Turn on two-factor authentication (SMS or Google Authenticator) under Security. BitTrade has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on a computer browser. BitTrade's API page cannot be opened from the phone app.
Go to My Page, then API, then Create API key (https://www.bittrade.co.jp/ja-jp/user/api/).
Type a note (備考) so you can tell your keys apart.
Add the IP address of the machine that runs your bot (up to 20). A key with no IP address set expires after 90 days.
Tick the permissions (see below), then press 秘密鍵を作成 (Create secret key).
Save the Access Key and Secret Key right away. BitTrade shows the Secret Key only once.
bittrade.permissions: BitTrade has three permissions: 読取 (Read), 取引 (Trade) and 出金 (Withdraw). New keys start with Read only, so also tick Trade. Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
bittrade.testnet_note: BitTrade has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITTRADE_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: BitTrade markets are priced in Japanese yen, so use ``JPY`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/JPY``).
Set an IP address on every bot key. BitTrade keys without an IP restriction stop working after 90 days, which can quietly break a long-running bot.
You can create at most 5 API keys. BitTrade's help pages and API docs are in Japanese.
BitTrade's API host is ``api-cloud.bittrade.co.jp``. CCXT uses it for you, so you do not need to set it.

bitvavo.summary: Bitvavo is a crypto exchange based in the Netherlands. It offers spot trading with prices in euros.
signup_steps: Create a Bitvavo account and finish identity verification.
Turn on two-factor authentication. Bitvavo will not let you create API keys without it.
Bitvavo has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on the website (keys cannot be made in the app), click your name and choose Settings.
Open the API tab and click Add new API key.
Enter a name and the IP address of your bot. Separate more than one IP with commas.
Choose the permissions (see below).
Enter your two-factor code and click Confirm. Save the key and secret right away; you cannot see the secret again.
bitvavo.permissions: Turn on View access and Trade digital assets. Bitvavo needs both to read your orders and trades. Leave Withdraw digital assets off: Bitvavo warns that API withdrawals skip two-factor and email checks.
bitvavo.testnet_note: Bitvavo has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BITVAVO_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``: a code config without it turns sandbox mode on, and CCXT then fails because Bitvavo has no test site.
extra_notes: Bitvavo markets are priced in euros, so use ``EUR`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/EUR``).
Bitvavo supports sub-accounts. An API key can be given access to sub-accounts and internal transfers, but a trading bot does not need those permissions.
sources: Bitvavo Help Center: What are API keys and how do I create them?

blofin.summary: BloFin is a crypto exchange best known for futures trading. Its API covers more than 200 perpetual contracts, plus copy trading, and BloFin also lists spot trading.
signup_steps: Go to the BloFin home page and select Sign up. Use an email address, phone number, Google account or Apple ID.
Enter the six digit code BloFin sends you within 5 minutes to finish creating the account.
Finish identity verification (open your avatar, then Identification) so your account gets higher limits.
api_key_steps: Log in on the BloFin website and open the APIs page (https://blofin.com/en/apis), then click Create an API Key.
Type a passphrase. You will need it every time the bot connects, so store it safely.
Choose the permissions (see below).
Link the IP address of the machine that runs your bot. Each key can have up to 20 IP addresses.
Save the API key, secret key and passphrase in a safe place.
blofin.permissions: Turn on READ and TRADE. TRADE lets the bot place and cancel orders. Leave TRANSFER off, and leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
blofin.testnet_note: BloFin runs a demo trading environment with simulated funds. Its API lives at https://demo-trading-openapi.blofin.com. Set ``BLOFIN_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to send LumiBot requests there.
extra_notes: BloFin needs three credentials: the API key, the secret key and the passphrase you typed. Put the passphrase in ``BLOFIN_API_PASSPHRASE`` (``"password"`` in a code config).
API keys that are not bound to an IP address expire after 90 days. Bind your bot's IP address so the key keeps working.
BloFin's own symbols use a dash, like ``BTC-USDT``. In LumiBot use the CCXT form ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the USDT perpetual.
Sub-accounts keep their own settings, separate from the main account. Common sub-accounts cannot withdraw.

BloFin Help Center: How to Register an Account on BloFin?
BloFin Help Center: How to Complete Identity Verification on BloFin?

btcmarkets.summary: BTC Markets is a spot crypto exchange where users buy and sell crypto with each other. Its markets are priced in Australian dollars (AUD), and it also lists some USDT markets.
signup_steps: Sign up for a BTC Markets account on https://www.btcmarkets.net.
Finish account verification. BTC Markets says your account must be verified before you can deposit, trade or withdraw.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for your BTC Markets account, and BTC Markets also recommends it for your email.
api_key_steps: Log in to your BTC Markets account.
Open the Account section from the main menu, select API Key and click Add new API key.
Name the key and choose the access level for each function of the key.
Review the details, click Submit and enter your password or 2FA code.
Copy the secret key right away. BTC Markets shows it only once. Your public API key is shown after that.
btcmarkets.permissions: BTC Markets sets access per function when you create the key. Give the trading functions Read & Write access so the bot can place and cancel orders, and give account functions read access so it can see balances. Leave anything that moves funds out (withdrawals or transfers) off. BTC Markets warns that Read & Write lets anyone with the secret key use every ability of that function.
btcmarkets.testnet_note: BTC Markets has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BTCMARKETS_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Use ``AUD`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/AUD``). CCXT also lists a ``BTC/USDT`` market.
If you lose your secret or think it leaked, click Revoke API Key on the same page and make a new key.
BTC Markets tracks API questions and bugs on its official GitHub at https://github.com/BTCMarkets/API/issues. The current API is v3, documented at https://docs.btcmarkets.net.
sources: BTC Markets Support: How to Access and Generate/Revoke Your API Keys
BTC Markets Support: Account Security on BTC Markets
BTC Markets Support: Help with the API

btcturk.summary: BtcTurk | Kripto is a crypto exchange with spot markets priced mostly in Turkish lira (TRY), plus USDT pairs. Its API covers market data, trading and account management.
signup_steps: Sign up in the BtcTurk | Kripto app with your email, mobile number and a password, then enter the codes sent to your email and phone.
Finish identity verification: scan your ID card, do the face check, fill in your profile and complete the short video call.
Set up two-step verification, for example an authenticator app, to protect your account.
api_key_steps: Log in on the BtcTurk | Kripto website. API keys can only be made on the website, not in the app.
Go to Account, then API Access (https://kripto.btcturk.com/en/account/api-access).
Click Create API Key (API Key Oluştur).
Choose the permissions (see below) and, if you like, limit the key to your bot's IP address.
Save the public key and private key in a safe place. If a key is ever shared by mistake, delete it at once and make a new one.
btcturk.permissions: Turn on Total Funds (Toplam Varlık) to read balances, Trade (Al-Sat) to place, check and cancel orders, and Account (Hesap) to read your trade history. WebSocket is only needed for live private streams. BtcTurk's API permission list has no withdrawal permission, so leave anything to do with withdrawals off and give the key only what the bot needs.
btcturk.testnet_note: BtcTurk has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``BTCTURK_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: BtcTurk writes pairs without a slash, like ``BTCTRY``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/TRY`` (or ``BTC/USDT``).
BtcTurk checks the request time against its server clock in milliseconds (UTC). Keep your bot machine's clock in sync, or signed requests will fail.
BtcTurk warns that too many failed sign-in requests can get your IP address blocked. Fix key errors before retrying in a loop.
You can turn a key off for a while or delete it from the API Access page.
