bullish.summary: Bullish is a regulated crypto exchange where you can buy, sell and trade digital assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. It offers spot and derivatives trading.
signup_steps: Create a Bullish account.
From the User Menu, choose Complete Account Verification and finish identity verification. Bullish says you cannot trade or deposit until this is done.
Register a two-factor authenticator, either a passkey (such as a hardware key) or a TOTP app.
api_key_steps: Log in to Bullish, click your account initials in the upper right corner, then click Settings.
Click API Keys, then Add API Key.
Choose HMAC as the API Key type. LumiBot (through CCXT) signs in with an HMAC key and secret.
Enter a name in the Key Name field and, if you want, add an IP whitelist with your bot's IP address.
Click Generate API Key and copy the key and secret somewhere safe.
bullish.permissions: Use an HMAC key for your bot. Bullish says HMAC keys only work on trading endpoints, while custody actions (deposits and withdrawals) need an ECDSA key. So an HMAC key can trade but cannot move money out. Do not give your bot an ECDSA key.
bullish.testnet_note: Bullish's docs mention sandbox and non-production environments, and CCXT's sandbox mode points at Bullish's SimNext test host (https://api.simnext.bullish-test.com). Bullish does not publish a public sign-up page for it, so contact Bullish support to get test access first. Then set ``BULLISH_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: If you add an IP whitelist to your key, Bullish only accepts login requests from inside that IP range. Add the address of every machine that runs your bot.
Bullish orders are placed in a trading account. By default CCXT uses your Primary trading account. To use another one, set the CCXT option ``tradingAccountId``.
Bullish spot markets are quoted in USDC (Bullish's own market name is ``BTCUSDC``, which is ``BTC/USDC`` in CCXT). Run CCXT ``load_markets()`` to see the exact symbols for perpetuals.
Bullish's sign-in tokens last 24 hours. CCXT logs in again for you, so you do not need to refresh anything by hand.
sources: Bullish Developer Docs: REST API Overview
Bullish Help Center: Steps to Complete Your KYC at Bullish
Bullish Help Center: Improving the safety and security of your Bullish account

bybit.summary: Bybit is a large crypto exchange for spot trading, perpetual and dated futures, and options. It has one of the most complete APIs in CCXT and is a CCXT certified exchange.
signup_steps: Create a Bybit account on the website and finish identity verification.
Wait if needed: Bybit may block API key creation for the first 48 hours after you register.
For practice, create a separate account on the Bybit testnet at https://testnet.bybit.com. Bybit also has a demo trading mode with its own keys; that is a different system from the testnet.
api_key_steps: Open API Management on the Bybit website (https://www.bybit.com/app/user/api-management). Keys cannot be made in the app.
Click Create New Key and pick System-generated API Keys.
Choose API Transaction and give the key a name.
Set the permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address.
Enter your two-factor code, then copy the key and secret and store them safely.
bybit.permissions: Choose Read-Write. Turn on the trade permissions for what you trade: spot trading, or contract orders and positions for perpetuals. Leave withdrawals off. Freqtrade's docs list Read-Write, Contract Orders and Contract Positions for futures bots.
bybit.testnet_note: Bybit's testnet lives at https://testnet.bybit.com and its API at https://api-testnet.bybit.com. Set ``BYBIT_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Bybit's demo trading mode is a different system with its own keys; the sandbox setting points at the testnet, not demo trading.
extra_notes: Bybit's Unified Trading Account keeps spot and derivatives in one wallet. Traders who connect bots often say to make sure it is turned on before you create keys.
CCXT has a separate exchange id, ``bybiteu``, for Bybit's EU site. It uses the api.bybit.eu API. Use the id that matches the site where you opened your account.
Run one bot per sub-account. Freqtrade warns that manual trades on the same account can confuse a bot.
sources: Bybit Help Center: How to create your API key
Bybit Learn: how to create and set up a Bybit API key
Practitioner video: automating TradingView alerts to Bybit (API key and Unified Trading steps)

bybiteu.summary: Bybit EU (bybit.eu) is Bybit's separate exchange site, run by Bybit EU GmbH. It offers spot trading in hundreds of cryptocurrencies, spot margin, EUR deposits and Earn products.
signup_steps: Register on the Bybit EU website or app with an email address or phone number. One email or phone number can open only one account.
Finish identity verification (ID document and a selfie) and set up Google Authenticator 2FA, which is required to create an API key.
For practice, register a separate account on the Bybit EU testnet at https://testnet.bybit.eu/App/register (PC browser only) and request test coins from Assets.
api_key_steps: On the Bybit EU website (keys cannot be made in the app), hover over your profile icon and click API to open API Management.
Click Create New Key and pick System-generated API Key (Bybit EU gives you a key and secret).
Choose API Transaction, give the key a clear name, and choose Read-Write.
Add your bot's IP address and select the permissions (see below).
Confirm with the email code and your Google Authenticator 2FA code.
Copy the API secret right away. Bybit EU shows it only once.
bybiteu.permissions: Choose Read-Write. Under Unified Trading, turn on Spot Trading (view, submit and cancel spot orders). Leave withdrawals off, and leave the Assets permissions (Account Transfer, Subaccount Transfer) off unless your bot needs them.
bybiteu.testnet_note: Bybit EU runs a testnet at https://testnet.bybit.eu with its API at https://api-testnet.bybit.eu. Testnet keys are made in the testnet account, and you can request test coins once every 24 hours. Set ``BYBITEU_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Bybit EU's demo trading mode is a different system with its own keys.
extra_notes: Use ``bybiteu`` only if your account is on bybit.eu. Accounts on bybit.com use the separate ``bybit`` exchange id, and keys from one site do not work on the other.
A key with no IP address bound to it expires after 90 days. Adding your bot's IP address removes that expiry, and one key can hold up to 100 IP addresses.
New accounts may not be able to create API keys for the first 48 hours after registration.
Bybit EU has spot pairs in EUR and USDC (for example ``BTC/EUR`` and ``BTC/USDC``), but no USDT pairs in CCXT's market list.
sources: Bybit EU Help Center: How to Create Your API Key
Bybit EU Learn: What is API trading and how to set it up on Bybit EU
Bybit EU Help Center: Everything You Need to Know to Get Started on Bybit EU
Bybit EU Help Center: How to Register for a Testnet Account and Request for Test Coins

cex.summary: CEX.IO is a crypto exchange that has run since 2013. Its Spot Trading platform has REST and WebSocket APIs for placing and canceling orders and reading market data.
signup_steps: Create a CEX.IO account and finish the identity verification CEX.IO asks for.
Turn on two-factor authentication. CEX.IO asks for a 2FA code when you create an API key.
CEX.IO has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to CEX.IO Spot Trading, click your name in the upper right corner, choose Profile and open API Keys Management.
Click + NEW API KEY and give the key a name.
Choose the permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address to the IP whitelist.
Click Create API Key and confirm with your 2FA code.
Save the API Secret from the pop-up right away. CEX.IO will not show it again.
Click Activate next to the new key and confirm with the code sent to your email. A new key does not work until you activate it.
cex.permissions: Turn on Read and Trade. Read lets the bot see your balances and orders, and Trade lets it place and cancel orders. Leave Funds Internal and Funds Wallet (shown as Funds External in the key list) off. A trading bot does not need to move money.
cex.testnet_note: CEX.IO has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``CEX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: If you edit a key's permissions or IP whitelist later, CEX.IO turns the key off. Click Activate and confirm by email again, or your bot will stop working.
If you leave the IP whitelist blank, the key works from any IP address. Adding your bot's IP is safer.
CEX.IO Spot Trading supports sub-accounts (five by default, more on request). A sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from your own.
CEX.IO lists BTC against several quote currencies, including USD, EUR, GBP, USDT and USDC. Use the quote currency you actually hold.
sources: CEX.IO Support: Profile page overview (+API trading guide)

coinbase.summary: Coinbase is a large crypto exchange. LumiBot trades through Coinbase Advanced, Coinbase's platform for more experienced traders, using the Advanced Trade API for spot crypto.
signup_steps: Create a Coinbase account with your email, confirm the email code, set a password and add your phone number.
Verify your identity. Coinbase asks for your legal name as it appears on your ID and has you upload the ID.
Set up 2-step verification. Then sign in to the Coinbase Developer Platform (CDP) at https://portal.cdp.coinbase.com with the same Coinbase account.
api_key_steps: In the CDP portal, open API Keys and select the Secret API Keys tab.
Click Create API key and enter a nickname.
Expand API restrictions and Advanced Settings. Add your bot's IP address to the IP allowlist (Coinbase recommends it), and pick the portfolio the key should trade.
Set the permissions (see below) and change the signature algorithm to ECDSA. ECDSA gives you a private key in the PEM format LumiBot expects.

Click Create API key. Copy the key name (it looks like ``organizations/<org-id>/apiKeys/<key-id>``) and the full private key from the window right away. The key file is no longer downloaded for you unless you click Download API key.
Set ``COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME`` to the key name and ``COINBASE_PRIVATE_KEY`` to the whole private key, from ``-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----`` to ``-----END EC PRIVATE KEY-----``.
coinbase.permissions: Turn on View and Trade. Coinbase's Advanced Trade docs show that reading accounts, orders and fills needs View, and placing and canceling orders needs Trade. Leave Transfer off. Coinbase warns that anyone who gets a key with the Transfer permission can send all the crypto out of your account.
coinbase.testnet_note: Coinbase Advanced has no sandbox for the Advanced Trade API in CCXT, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``COINBASE_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: The private key is several lines long. Keep the line breaks: either paste it as a multi-line value in quotes, or write it on one line with ``\n`` where each line break goes. Coinbase's docs say the newlines must be kept for the key to work.
Each CDP key is tied to one portfolio. If you want a bot to trade a separate portfolio, make a key for that portfolio. This also keeps bot trades apart from your manual trades.
New CDP keys do not use a passphrase. ``COINBASE_API_PASSPHRASE`` is only for old legacy keys, so leave it unset.

This page is for Coinbase Advanced (CCXT id ``coinbase``). Coinbase Exchange and Coinbase International Exchange are separate CCXT ids (``coinbaseexchange`` and ``coinbaseinternational``) with their own key systems that use a passphrase.
sources: Coinbase Developer Platform: Coinbase App API Key Authentication
Coinbase Developer Platform: CDP API key types and algorithms
Coinbase Developer Platform: Advanced Trade API endpoints and key permissions
Coinbase Developer Platform: Welcome to Advanced Trade API
Coinbase Help: New customer resource guide

coinbaseexchange.summary: Coinbase Exchange is Coinbase's spot exchange for businesses and qualified individuals, with REST, FIX and WebSocket APIs for trading and market data. Coinbase says most individuals should use a regular Coinbase.com account instead.
signup_steps: Apply for a Coinbase Exchange account at https://accounts.coinbase.com/pick-your-account. Coinbase's onboarding team reviews the application and contacts you with next steps.

When approved, open the email from Coinbase, create your password and sign in. You must set up 2-step verification with a mobile phone number the first time; Coinbase recommends a security key or Google Authenticator after that.
For practice, also create a separate account on the Coinbase Exchange sandbox at https://public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com. Sandbox logins and keys are separate from your real account.
api_key_steps: Sign in to the Exchange dashboard (https://exchange.coinbase.com/) and select API at the bottom of the left sidebar.
Select + New API Key in the top-right corner.
Choose the Portfolio the bot will trade in. Each key works with one portfolio only.
Pick the permissions (see below) and create a passphrase.
Enter the IP address of the machine that runs your bot. Coinbase requires an IP whitelist; separate more than one address with commas.
Select Create API Key and confirm with 2-step verification. Save the key, secret and passphrase right away; Coinbase shows the secret and passphrase only once and cannot recover them.
coinbaseexchange.permissions: Turn on View and Trade. Leave Transfer off: Coinbase says a Transfer key can move money in and out of your account and skips 2-step verification. Leave Manage off too, since a bot does not need to change account settings.
coinbaseexchange.testnet_note: Coinbase Exchange runs a public sandbox at https://public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com with fake funds you can add yourself. It has only some of the real order books, and you must make separate API keys there (profile menu, API, New API Key). Set ``COINBASEEXCHANGE_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: Coinbase Exchange keys need three values: the key, the secret and the passphrase you chose. In CCXT the passphrase is called ``password``.
This page is for Coinbase Exchange (CCXT id ``coinbaseexchange``). A regular Coinbase.com account with Advanced Trade uses the separate ``coinbase`` id and Coinbase Developer Platform keys instead.
Your computer clock must be within 30 seconds of Coinbase's server time, or Coinbase rejects the request as expired. Keep the clock synced.

Each key is tied to one portfolio (profile). To keep a key from reading other portfolios, turn on portfolio isolation under Settings, Security. Using a separate portfolio per bot keeps bot trades apart.
sources: Coinbase Help: How to create an API key (Exchange)
Coinbase Help: Onboarding to Coinbase Exchange
Coinbase Help: Getting started with your Exchange account
Coinbase Developer docs: Exchange REST API authentication

coincheck.summary: Coincheck is a crypto exchange run by Coincheck, Inc. It has a simple buy and sell desk and the Coincheck exchange, an order book for spot trading. Its API places and cancels orders on the exchange and checks your balance.
signup_steps: Open a personal account in the Coincheck app. Coincheck asks you to set up a passkey and agree to its terms.
Submit your identity document and basic details, then wait for Coincheck's review to finish.
Set up two-step authentication with an authenticator app. Coincheck asks for its code when you create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the API page (https://coincheck.com/api_settings). You can also click the gear icon, then API Keys.
Click Add a new API key.
Under API key permissions, check the boxes the bot needs (see below). Enter the IP address of the machine that runs your bot, or leave it blank.
Type the same password you use to log in to Coincheck and click OK.
Enter the code from your authenticator app.
Copy the Access key and Secret Access key and keep them private.
coincheck.permissions: Check the boxes for the order functions (new order, unsettled order list, cancel order, order transactions) and for account balance. Leave the send crypto and withdraw boxes off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
coincheck.testnet_note: Coincheck has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``COINCHECK_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Coincheck needs only two credentials: the Access key (``COINCHECK_API_KEY``) and the Secret Access key (``COINCHECK_API_SECRET``). There is no passphrase.
Coincheck lets you limit each key to IP addresses you choose. Add your server's IP so a leaked key cannot be used from somewhere else.
If a key fails with a missing permission error, edit it and check the permission boxes again. Coincheck says a key with the wrong boxes cannot connect.
sources: Coincheck FAQ: APIキー（アクセスキー、シークレットアクセスキー）の取得方法を教えてください (How to get an API key)
Coincheck FAQ: 口座開設の流れを教えてください (Account opening steps)
Coincheck FAQ: アプリから口座開設する方法を教えてください (Open an account in the app)

coinex.summary: CoinEx is a crypto exchange for spot trading and futures. Its v2 API serves both spot and futures markets from one base address.
signup_steps: Create a CoinEx account on the website or app.
Turn on two-factor authentication (SMS, an authenticator app or a passkey). CoinEx asks for a 2FA code when you create an API key.
CoinEx has no testnet, so plan to start with a very small trade.
api_key_steps: Log in at https://www.coinex.com, click your avatar in the top right corner and pick API Management.
Click Create API.
Enter an API Remark (a name for the key) and the Applicable IP address: the public IP of the machine running your bot. You can list up to 50 addresses, one per line.
Tick Trade. Leave Withdraw unticked.
Enter your 2FA code (SMS, authenticator app or passkey) and click Create.
Copy the Access ID (your API key) and Secret Key. The key starts working within 10 to 15 minutes.
coinex.permissions: Tick Trade so the bot can place and cancel orders. Leave Withdraw unticked. A trading bot never needs to move money out of your account.
coinex.testnet_note: CoinEx has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``COINEX_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bind a fixed IP address. CoinEx says a key with no fixed IP expires after 90 days, and you must click Renew on the API Management page to keep it working.
If you see an IP Prohibited error, your bot's IP is not on the key's list. If you see access_id not exist right after making a key, wait about 10 minutes and try again.
CoinEx calls the API key the Access ID. Put it in ``COINEX_API_KEY`` and the Secret Key in ``COINEX_API_SECRET``. No passphrase is needed.
A main account can create up to 20 sub-accounts. CoinEx suggests them for running separate strategies, so each bot can have its own sub-account and key.
sources: CoinEx Help: What's API, How to Set it Up and Extend Its Validity Period
CoinEx Help: Introduction to CoinEx Sub-account

coinmate.summary: Coinmate is a crypto exchange run by COINMATE a.s. It offers spot trading between crypto and fiat money, with markets priced in euros (EUR) and Czech koruna (CZK).
signup_steps: Apply for a Coinmate account on https://coinmate.io and verify your email address.
Provide the identity details Coinmate asks for. You can deposit, trade and withdraw once Coinmate approves your account.
Set up Google Authenticator if you want to use it. Coinmate asks you to confirm API changes with an email code or a Google Authenticator code.
api_key_steps: Log in and open Account, then API (https://coinmate.io/account/api). API access is off until you turn it on there.
Note your client ID, which is shown on the same page.
Generate a new API key pair. You get a public key and a private key.
Choose the access level (trading only), then confirm the change with your email code or Google Authenticator code.
Store the private key somewhere safe and never share it. Anyone with your keys and client ID can use your API access.
coinmate.permissions: Coinmate has two API levels: one for remote trading only, and one that also allows withdrawals. Pick the trading-only level for a bot and leave withdrawals off. Coinmate warns that a key with withdrawals can move money without the usual email or Google Authenticator check.
coinmate.testnet_note: Coinmate has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``COINMATE_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Coinmate needs three values: the public key goes in ``COINMATE_API_KEY``, the private key in ``COINMATE_API_SECRET`` and your client ID in ``COINMATE_UID`` (CCXT's ``uid`` field). Every private request is signed with all three.

Coinmate requires each request with a key pair to use a larger nonce than the one before. If two programs share one key pair, requests can arrive out of order and Coinmate answers access denied. Give each bot its own key pair (Coinmate lets one account create several).
Coinmate asks for no more than 100 requests per minute and says it will ban the IP address of clients that go over.
Markets are priced in EUR and CZK, for example ``BTC/EUR`` or ``BTC/CZK``.
sources: Coinmate Trading Portal API documentation (Security, Request limits)
Coinmate Terms and Conditions (sections 3 Account opening and 24 API)
Coinmate official API examples on GitHub (credentials and account API page)

coinone.summary: Coinone is a crypto exchange with spot markets priced in Korean won (KRW). Its Open API gives market data, balances, order history and trading.
signup_steps: Sign up in the Coinone app with identity verification (Kakao Bank or phone verification).
Finish the remaining checks Coinone asks for: ID photo, personal details and linking your own bank account.
Add extra channel authentication (Kakao or Naver simple authentication) to protect your account.
api_key_steps: Log in on the Coinone website, scroll to the footer and click Open API.
Open Integrated API Management (통합 API 관리) and go to the Personal API (개인용 API) section.
Click Issue New Key (새로운 키 발급).
Choose the permissions (see below) and enter the public IPv4 address of your bot. Coinone requires at least one IP and allows up to 5 per key.
Save the Access Token and Secret Key in a safe place. If you lose them you must issue a new key.
coinone.permissions: Turn on balance inquiry (잔고 조회), order inquiry (주문 조회) and order management (주문 관리), which lets the key place and cancel buy and sell orders. Leave withdrawal (출금 권한) off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
coinone.testnet_note: Coinone has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``COINONE_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Coinone API keys expire one year after you create them. Check the expiry date on the API management page and make a new key before it runs out.
Coinone calls the API key an Access Token. Put the Access Token in the API key field and the Secret Key in the secret field.
Use a fixed IP address for your bot. Coinone blocks calls from IPs that are not on the key's list, so a changing home IP can break your bot.
CCXT's Coinone support has no market orders (only limit orders), so use limit orders with this exchange.

Coinone support: Open API FAQ (key expiry, IP whitelisting)
