coinsph.summary: Coins.ph is an e-wallet and crypto app where you can buy and sell crypto in pesos (PHP). Its Spot Trade exchange offers PHP and crypto trading pairs, and that is what LumiBot trades on.
signup_steps: Create a Coins.ph account.
Finish ID and selfie verification (or higher). Coins.ph requires this before you can create an API key.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Coins.ph will not let you create an API key or a sub-account without it.
api_key_steps: Log in to Coins.ph on the website, click your profile in the lower left and open Account Settings.
Under the Security section, click Manage next to API Management.
Click Create API at the top and enter API Remarks (a name for the key).
Enter your Google Authenticator (2FA) code.
Copy the Secret right away. Coins.ph shows it only once. If you lose it, you must delete the key and make a new one.
Click Bind IP Whitelist and add the IP address of your bot. Each key needs at least 1 and at most 5 whitelisted IP addresses.
coinsph.permissions: Coins.ph API keys list their access as Read only, Enable Spot, Enable Convert, Enable Crypto Wallet, Enable Fiat and Enable Account. For a trading bot, turn on Enable Spot. Leave Enable Crypto Wallet and Enable Fiat off, and keep withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
coinsph.testnet_note: Coins.ph has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``COINSPH_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Each Coins.ph account can create only 1 API key. If you need more, use sub-accounts: a main account can have up to 30, each with its own API key.
Coins.ph sub-accounts can only trade through the API, and their trade history is only visible through the API, not the website. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from your own.
Coins.ph Spot Trade markets are quoted in PHP, USDT or USDC, for example ``BTC/PHP`` or ``BTC/USDT``. Minimum order sizes vary by pair.
sources: Coins.ph Help Center: How to set up API for Spot Trade?
Coins.ph Help Center: How can I trade using sub-accounts?
Coins.ph Help Center: Frequently Asked Questions about Sub-Account
Coins.ph Help Center: How do I trade in Spot Trade?
Coins.ph REST API documentation (Api Key information)

coinspot.summary: CoinSpot is a crypto exchange where you buy, sell and swap cryptocurrencies. Its markets are priced mostly in AUD, with some USDT markets, and LumiBot uses it for spot trading.
signup_steps: Register on coinspot.com.au or in the CoinSpot app with your email address and a password, then confirm your email.
Verify your account: enter your personal details and upload an identity document.
Turn on app based 2FA: My Account menu, Security, Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), Enable Two Factor Authentication. CoinSpot needs it to create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the My Account menu, then API (https://www.coinspot.com.au/my/api).
Select Generate New API Key and enter a name for the key.
Choose the API Key Type (see below), enter your 2FA token and select Create API Key.
Open the confirmation email and click the link in the same browser and device you are using.
Tap View Secret (One Time Only) and copy the secret. It disappears once you leave the API page.
coinspot.permissions: CoinSpot has two key types: Read Only and Full Access. A trading bot needs Full Access, because a Read Only key cannot place orders. Coin withdrawals must be turned on separately in the API key options, so leave that option off. A bot never needs to move coins out of your account.
coinspot.testnet_note: CoinSpot has no sandbox or testnet. Test with a very small amount on your real account, leave ``COINSPOT_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: In CCXT, CoinSpot supports limit orders only (no market orders). Use limit orders in your strategy, for example ``BTC/AUD`` at a set price.
CoinSpot allows 1000 API requests per minute.
CoinSpot help pages warn to give third-party tools (such as tax software) a Read Only key, never Full Access. Make a separate Full Access key just for your bot.
If you lose the secret, delete the key with Delete API Key and generate a new one.
sources: CoinSpot Help: How to set up API Key
CoinSpot Help: How to set up 2FA
CoinSpot Help: Mobile App, Register and Verify a Personal Account

cryptocom.summary: Crypto.com Exchange is the trading platform from Crypto.com. It says you can trade 350+ assets, and its API covers spot and derivatives trading.
signup_steps: Create a Crypto.com Exchange account and finish the sign-up checks it asks for.
Turn on two-factor authentication. You need the 2FA code to create an API key.
Crypto.com's test site (UAT) is invite only for institutional accounts, so most people test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to the Crypto.com Exchange website.
Click your profile in the top right, then Manage Account, then API Management.
Choose Create a new API key, give it a label and enter your 2FA code.
Turn on Enable Trading and add the IP address of the machine that runs your bot.
Copy the secret key right away. Crypto.com shows it only when the key is created.
cryptocom.permissions: New keys start with Can Read only. Add Enable Trading. Leave Enable Withdrawal off. Crypto.com requires an IP whitelist as soon as you turn on trading or withdrawals.
cryptocom.testnet_note: Crypto.com runs a UAT sandbox at https://uat-api.3ona.co/exchange/v1, but access is by invitation only for institutional accounts. If you have access, set ``CRYPTOCOM_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Otherwise test with a very small amount and leave the sandbox off.
extra_notes: Use an Exchange API key. The Agent Key in the Crypto.com App is a different product for AI agents and is not the Exchange API key CCXT uses.
If you lose the secret key, create a new API key. Crypto.com cannot show it again.
Spot pairs look like ``BTC/USD``. Crypto.com perpetuals use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USD:USD``.
sources: Crypto.com Exchange API v1: common API reference
Crypto.com Help Center: API Key Management (App Agent Key)

cryptomus.summary: Cryptomus is a crypto payment gateway that also runs a spot exchange. Its personal (user) API lets you check trading wallet balances and create, list and cancel exchange orders.
signup_steps: Create a Cryptomus personal account.
Bind two-factor authentication in Settings. Cryptomus asks you to do this before you generate a User API key.
Cryptomus has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the Settings section of your personal account.
Bind two-factor authentication if you have not done it yet.
Go to the User API key section and click Generate.
Copy the API key and store it safely.
Click your user icon to find your user UUID. Cryptomus signs every personal API request with this UUID plus the API key, so you need both.
cryptomus.permissions: Cryptomus's docs show no permission choices for the User API key, so treat it like a full-access key and keep it private. Do not use your payment or payout keys for trading: Cryptomus issues separate keys for accepting payments and making payouts, and a trading bot only needs the User API key.
cryptomus.testnet_note: Cryptomus has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``CRYPTOMUS_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Cryptomus uses two credentials, not the usual key and secret pair. In CCXT terms, your User API key is the ``secret`` and your user UUID is the ``uid``. There is no separate ``apiKey`` value.
CCXT supports limit orders on Cryptomus but not market orders, so have your strategy place limit orders.
Cryptomus writes pairs like ``TRX_USDT`` in its own API. LumiBot and CCXT use the ``BTC/USDT`` form.
sources: Cryptomus API docs: Getting API keys
Cryptomus API docs: Request format (userId and sign headers)
Cryptomus API docs: Limit order creation

deribit.summary: Deribit is a crypto derivatives exchange, running since 2016, best known for bitcoin and ether options. It offers options, perpetuals, futures and spot trading, and it runs a separate test platform.
signup_steps: Click Create account on www.deribit.com and sign up with email, Google or Apple. Confirm your email with the link Deribit sends you.

Set up two-factor authentication (a passkey or an authenticator app), which Deribit requires for every user. Then complete identity verification (KYC), which Deribit needs before you can trade without limits.
For practice, also create a separate account on the Deribit test platform at https://test.deribit.com. Test accounts and keys are separate from your real account.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the API section in the Account panel at the top right.
Press Add new key.
Choose Deribit-generated key (the simple choice). Self-generated keys use your own key pair.
Pick the scopes (see below), enter a name, and add the IP address of your bot under IP Whitelisting.
Save the Client ID and Client Secret right away. Deribit shows the Client Secret only once. In LumiBot the Client ID is your API key and the Client Secret is your secret.
deribit.permissions: Give the key trade:read_write (place and change orders) and account:read and wallet:read (read your account and balances). Leave wallet at read only, never wallet:read_write, because that scope allows withdrawals. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
deribit.testnet_note: Deribit runs a full test platform at https://test.deribit.com with its own accounts and API keys, so a key from www.deribit.com will not work there. Set ``DERIBIT_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to send LumiBot requests there.
extra_notes: Deribit's own instrument names look like ``BTC-PERPETUAL``. In LumiBot use the CCXT form: spot is ``BTC/USDC``, the USDC perpetual is ``BTC/USDC:USDC`` and the inverse bitcoin perpetual is ``BTC/USD:BTC``.

A main account can create subaccounts. Each one keeps its own collateral, positions and up to 8 API keys, and subaccount keys only work on that subaccount. A subaccount per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
API rate limits on Deribit depend on how much the account trades, and each subaccount has its own limits.
Deribit is now run with Coinbase. Deribit's sign-up page may send you to Coinbase onboarding instead; if it does, follow those steps.
sources: Deribit Support: How to register on Deribit
Deribit API docs: Creating API keys
Coinbase Help: International Exchange and Deribit Integration FAQs

digifinex.summary: DigiFinex is a trading platform for crypto assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. Its API covers spot and margin trading, plus perpetual swaps through a separate swap API.
signup_steps: Open https://www.digifinex.com and click Sign Up. Enter your email address or phone number and click Create Account.
Enter the verification code DigiFinex sends you and click Activate Account.
Turn on Google two-factor authentication (User Profile, then 2Factor Authentication). DigiFinex requires 2FA before you can create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in at https://www.digifinex.com, move your mouse to the head icon in the top right corner and choose User Center.
Scroll down to API Setting and click Create API.
Fill in Name your API and click Send Code to get a code by email.
Enter the email code and your 2FA code, then click Confirm.
Copy the Api Key and Api Secret right away. DigiFinex shows them only once. If you click away first, you must make a new key.
Bind your bot's IP address to the key for safety. DigiFinex lets you bind up to 4 IP addresses to each key.
digifinex.permissions: DigiFinex's guide does not list the permission names. Its API docs say each key has a permission setting, so check that the key is allowed to trade. Leave withdrawals off if you see that option. A trading bot never needs to move money out of your account.
digifinex.testnet_note: DigiFinex has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``DIGIFINEX_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Each DigiFinex user can create up to 5 API keys, and each key can be bound to up to 4 IP addresses.

DigiFinex uses two API bases: ``https://openapi.digifinex.com/v3`` for spot and margin, and ``https://openapi.digifinex.com/swap/v2`` for perpetual swaps. CCXT handles both under the ``digifinex`` id.
DigiFinex supports sub-accounts. A normal account can make 1 sub-account, and the limit grows with VIP level. A sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual ones.
If you get an ``IP address Unauthorized`` error, your bot's IP is not bound to the key.
sources: DigiFinex Help: How to Establish your DigiFinex API Address?
DigiFinex Help: How to register an account
DigiFinex Help: How to set up 2FA

dydx.summary: dYdX is a self-custody (decentralized) trading platform built on its own blockchain, dYdX Chain. It focuses on perpetual futures settled in USDC, and you trade from your own wallet instead of handing coins to a company.
signup_steps: Open https://dydx.trade and connect your wallet. When you sign with your Ethereum wallet, dYdX creates your dYdX Chain address and its secret phrase.
Add funds to your dYdX account. Positions are margined and settled in USDC.
For practice, use the dYdX testnet at https://v4.testnet.dydx.exchange. Testnet funds come from the faucet at https://faucet.v4testnet.dydx.exchange and only work on testnet.
api_key_steps: Use a separate Ethereum wallet just for the bot, holding only the money you want it to trade.
Connect that wallet on https://dydx.trade and sign. dYdX creates your dYdX Chain address and secret phrase from that signature.
Copy your dYdX address (it starts with dydx1). You can see it by clicking your address in the upper right corner.
Export the private key of that Ethereum wallet from your wallet app. CCXT uses it to rebuild the same dYdX key.
dYdX also offers API Trading Keys (More, then API Trading Keys, then Generate New API Key) that cannot withdraw. CCXT's dYdX connector does not use them yet, so LumiBot needs the wallet key above.
dydx.permissions: dYdX API Trading Keys made in the app can only trade with your cross margin, and dYdX says they cannot withdraw funds or move assets. CCXT's dYdX connector does not support those keys yet. It signs with your account's own key, which has full control, including withdrawals. That is why you should use a separate wallet that holds only the money you want the bot to trade, and never share its private key or secret phrase.
dydx.testnet_note: dYdX runs a public testnet with its own site at https://v4.testnet.dydx.exchange and a faucet at https://faucet.v4testnet.dydx.exchange. Set ``DYDX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: With environment variables, set ``DYDX_WALLET_ADDRESS`` to your dYdX Chain address (it starts with ``dydx1``, not your Ethereum ``0x`` address) and ``DYDX_PRIVATE_KEY`` to the private key of the Ethereum wallet you connected.
dYdX markets are perpetual futures settled in USDC, so use the full CCXT symbol, for example ``BTC/USDC:USDC``.
dYdX warns that anyone who knows your secret phrase can send, trade and sell from that account. Store keys offline and never paste them into chats. Use separate keys for each bot.
Mainnet data comes from the indexer at https://indexer.dydx.trade/v4, and the testnet indexer is https://indexer.v4testnet.dydx.exchange.
sources: dYdX Help Center: API Trading Keys (Permissioned Keys)
dYdX Docs: Connecting to dYdX (endpoints, testnet faucet)
dYdX Help Center: Secret Phrase on dYdX Chain

extended.summary: Extended is a decentralized exchange with leveraged perpetual markets on crypto and real-world assets, plus crypto spot trading against USDC. You sign in with your own crypto wallet.
signup_steps: Open Extended and connect a wallet. Extended works with EVM and Starknet wallets.
Sign the account creation request, then sign the registration request. This creates your Extended trading account and turns on trading.
For practice, also connect a wallet on the Extended testnet at https://starknet.sepolia.extended.exchange and claim free test USDC (up to $1,000 worth per wallet per day).
api_key_steps: Log in to Extended with your wallet.
Pick the sub-account (trading account) you want the bot to use. You can make up to 10 per wallet from the Account section at the bottom right of the Trade screen.
Open the API management page (https://app.extended.exchange/api-management).
Create or copy the API key for that sub-account.
Copy the Stark private key for the same sub-account. LumiBot sends it to CCXT as ``privateKey`` to sign orders. Never share it with anyone.
extended.permissions: Extended has no permission checkboxes. The API key alone can only read data: Extended says it cannot create orders, transfer funds or withdraw. Orders need the API key plus a signature from the Stark private key, and so do withdrawals. Extended only sends withdrawals to wallets linked to your account, but treat the Stark private key like a password and keep only bot money in the bot's sub-account.
extended.testnet_note: Extended runs a testnet at https://starknet.sepolia.extended.exchange with its own accounts and keys, and free test USDC from the Claim button in the Account section. Set ``EXTENDED_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: Each Extended sub-account has its own API key and Stark key. Use a separate sub-account for each bot so its money and trades stay apart.
Perpetual symbols use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDC:USDC``. Spot is plain ``BTC/USDC``. Spot always trades at 1x leverage.

Extended moved its settlement network from Starknet to Arc (a blockchain from Circle) starting 22 October 2026. Extended says you keep the same wallet and keys. If your bot cannot connect after the move, check that your CCXT version is current.
sources: Extended Docs: Migration from Starknet to Arc

fmfwio.summary: FMFW.io is a crypto exchange for spot trading, margin trading and perpetual futures. Its API v3 covers spot, margin and futures trading plus wallet management.
signup_steps: Create an account on fmfw.io and confirm your email address.

Turn on 2FA: click Settings, open the Security tab (https://fmfw.io/settings/security), click Add GAuth, save the backup code and confirm with the email link within 10 minutes. Email plus 2FA gives you the default Individual level.
For higher withdrawal limits, verify for Individual Pro on the KYC tab (https://fmfw.io/settings/know-your-customer) with a photo ID and a selfie. FMFW.io says this can take up to 24 hours.
api_key_steps: Log in, open Settings and go to the API Settings page. FMFW.io's API docs say this is where keys are made.
Create a new API key. You can have several keys, each with its own access rights.
Choose the access rights (see below).
Copy the API key and secret key and store them safely. LumiBot needs both.
fmfwio.permissions: Turn on the "Orderbook, History, Trading balance" and "Place/cancel orders" access rights. Leave "Withdraw cryptocurrencies" and "Payment information" off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
fmfwio.testnet_note: FMFW.io's own docs do not describe a sandbox or testnet. CCXT's sandbox setting for fmfwio points at a HitBTC demo server (api.demo.hitbtc.com), which is not an FMFW.io service, so do not use it. Test with a very small amount on your real account, leave ``FMFWIO_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: FMFW.io keeps a wallet balance and a separate trading balance. Move funds into your trading balance before the bot starts, or it will see no money to trade with.
Sub-accounts are a good way to give each bot its own funds. Each sub-account needs its own email and its own 2FA, and withdrawals are off on sub-accounts by default.
Keep polling modest. FMFW.io's default REST limit is 20 requests per second per IP (30 burst), and an account can have at most 2000 open orders per symbol.
The REST API lives at https://api.fmfw.io/api/3 and uses Basic authentication with your API key and secret.
sources: FMFW.io Help Center: How to verify my account?

foxbit.summary: Foxbit is a crypto exchange where you can buy, sell and trade the coins it lists, with prices in reais (BRL).
signup_steps: Go to https://app.foxbit.com.br/ (or the Foxbit app), click Cadastre-se and enter your email and a strong password.
Click Verificar E-mail in the message Foxbit sends, choose a personal account, and fill in your personal details and address.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Foxbit requires it before you can add an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in on the desktop site and click Configurações da conta (account settings) in the top right.
Click API Key, then click Próximo (next).
Choose the permissions, give the key a name and click Criar API Key.
Enter your 2FA code if asked.
Save the key and secret right away. Foxbit will not show the secret again after you close the window.
foxbit.permissions: Turn on read and trade. Foxbit's API docs list read, trade, deposit and withdrawal, and order endpoints need trade. Leave withdrawal off. Foxbit also requires an IP list for any key with withdrawals.
foxbit.testnet_note: Foxbit has no sandbox, and its API docs say requests run against the real environment. Test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``FOXBIT_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Foxbit offers two kinds of keys: one Foxbit generates (key plus secret) and one where you upload your own Ed25519 public key. CCXT signs with a secret, so create the standard key Foxbit generates.
Foxbit writes markets without a separator, like ``btcbrl``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/BRL``.
If you lose the key details, delete the key and make a new one.
sources: Foxbit FAQ: O que é API Key e como utilizar?
Foxbit FAQ: Como criar uma API Key com chaves assimétricas

gate.summary: Gate is a large crypto exchange that covers more than 5,400 crypto assets. Its API v4 supports spot, margin, perpetual and delivery futures, and options trading.
signup_steps: Create a Gate account on the website and finish account verification.
Set up your fund password and two-factor authentication. Gate asks for both before you can create an API key.
For practice, Gate also offers testnet API keys (see the testnet note below). Testnet keys only work on the testnet, and real keys do not work there.
api_key_steps: Log in on the Gate website, hover over the profile icon at the top and click API Management.
Click Create API Key and choose API v4 Key as the key type (API v2 keys are spot only).
Enter a remark to name the key and bind the IP address of the machine that runs your bot.
Choose the account type (Classic Account, Margin Trading or Testnet), set the permissions and pick the currency pairs, then click Submit.
Read the risk reminder, click I accept, enter your fund password and two-factor code, and click Confirm.
Copy the key and secret and store them safely.
gate.permissions: Choose Read and Write for the markets your bot trades, for example spot read/write, and futures read/write only if you trade futures. One API v4 key can hold several of these permissions. Leave withdrawals off. Gate API keys can withdraw if you allow it, and a bot never needs to move money out of your account.
gate.testnet_note: Gate runs a testnet. Create a separate key with the Testnet account type in API Management (futures testnet keys are made under their own TestNet tab). The testnet API lives at https://api-testnet.gateapi.io/api/v4. Set ``GATE_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: Bind an IP address to your key. Gate keys with no IP binding accept requests from any address and expire after 90 days.
Gate API v4 keys can be limited to certain currency pairs when you create them. If you use this, include every pair your bot trades.
Gate rate limits are counted for each main account and each sub-account separately, so a sub-account per bot also keeps one bot from slowing another.
CCXT also has a separate ``gateeu`` id. For an account on gate.com, use ``gate``.
sources: Gate Help Center: How to Create and Manage API Keys on Gate (Web)

gateeu.summary: Gate EU (Gate Europe) is the European platform of the Gate crypto exchange. It offers spot trading, convert, staking and euro funding.
signup_steps: Create a Gate EU account at https://www.gate.com/en-eu/signup.
Finish account verification. Gate asks for this before you can create API keys.
Set a fund password and turn on two-factor authentication. Gate needs both to confirm a new API key.
api_key_steps: Log in, hover over the profile icon and choose API Management (Gate's docs call this account management, then APIv4 keys).
Click Create API Key and choose an API v4 key.
Add a note (remark) and, if your bot has a fixed IP address, bind the key to it.
Set the permissions (see below) and pick the currency pairs the key may trade.
Read and accept the risk reminder, then enter your fund password and 2FA code to confirm.
Copy the API key and secret and store them somewhere safe.
gateeu.permissions: Gate EU groups permissions into spot, wallet and withdrawal, and each can be off, read-only or read-write. For a trading bot, set spot to read-write. Leave withdrawal off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
gateeu.testnet_note: Gate EU's API docs do not describe a testnet for Gate EU accounts, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``GATEEU_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Gate EU has its own API host, ``https://api.gateeu.com/api/v4``, hosted in Paris. Use the ``gateeu`` id with keys from your Gate EU account. The global Gate site uses a separate CCXT id, ``gate``.
If you do not bind an IP address, Gate's help says the key works from any address but expires after 90 days. Bind your bot's IP (up to 20 IPv4 addresses per key) to avoid a surprise expiry.
Gate writes pairs as ``BTC_EUR``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/EUR``. Gate EU also lists USDC pairs such as ``BTC/USDC``.
Each Gate account can hold several API v4 keys with separate permissions, so you can give each bot its own key.
sources: Gate Help: How to Create and Manage API Keys on Gate (Web)

gemini.summary: Gemini is a crypto exchange that offers spot crypto trading, perpetuals, margin and staking, with REST, WebSocket and FIX APIs.
signup_steps: Sign up for a Gemini account at https://exchange.gemini.com/.
Verify your identity by uploading a clear photo ID. Gemini only lets fully verified accounts create API keys.

For practice, also register a separate account on the Gemini demo environment at https://exchange.sandbox.gemini.com. Gemini fills new demo accounts with test balances, and demo keys only work in the demo environment.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the API settings page (https://exchange.gemini.com/settings/api).
Click Create a new API Key.
Choose the scope: the single account the bot should trade in (most people have one account called Primary). Avoid the Master scope, which reaches every account you have.
Choose the Trading role (see below).
Under IP Allow List pick Trusted IPs Only and add the IP address of the machine that runs your bot. Gemini recommends this for every key.
Copy the API key and API secret and keep the secret private, like a password.
gemini.permissions: Use the Trading role (Gemini also calls it Trader). It can check balances, place and cancel orders and view orders and trades. Do not add Fund Management, which can withdraw crypto, and leave the Master scope and Administrator role alone. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
gemini.testnet_note: Gemini runs a full demo environment (sandbox) at https://exchange.sandbox.gemini.com with test funds and simulated order book activity. Make a separate account and API key there. Set ``GEMINI_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: A Gemini API key that is not used for 180 days expires and stops working. If a bot sits idle for months, plan to make a new key.
Give each bot its own key. Gemini says each application should have its own key so permissions stay separate.
Spot is plain ``BTC/USD``. Gemini perpetuals trade in a separate derivatives account and appear in CCXT as ``BTC/GUSD:GUSD``; you move funds there from your exchange account.
When you create a key, Gemini lets you pick a nonce mode. Time-based nonces need your computer clock within 30 seconds of Gemini's server time, so keep the clock synced.
sources: Gemini Support: How do I create an API key?
Gemini Support: Why am I unable to create an API key?
Gemini Support: How do I verify my identity in the app?
Gemini Support: derivatives account vs exchange account
Gemini Developer docs: API key authentication

hashkey.summary: HashKey Global is a crypto exchange. Its API covers spot trading and perpetual futures such as BTCUSDT-PERPETUAL.
signup_steps: Create a HashKey Global account on the website.
Finish identity verification (KYC) with a passport or government ID that does not expire within three months.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). For practice, you can also ask HashKey for a sandbox account by emailing global-api@hashkey.com.
api_key_steps: Log in on the HashKey Global website.
Open Settings (top right), then API Management.
Click Create API.
Enter a name for the key, pick the permission and set an IP access restriction for your bot's machine.
Copy the Access Key and Secret Key and store them safely.
hashkey.permissions: Choose READ/WRITE so the bot can place and cancel orders. READ-ONLY is only for looking up orders and trades. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
hashkey.testnet_note: HashKey Global runs a public sandbox at https://global.sim.hashkeydev.com with its API at https://api-glb.sim.hashkeydev.com. Get a sandbox account by emailing global-api@hashkey.com, then make sandbox keys there. Set ``HASHKEY_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: HashKey Global needs only two credentials: the Access Key (``HASHKEY_API_KEY``) and the Secret Key (``HASHKEY_API_SECRET``). There is no passphrase.
In the sandbox, every 2FA, SMS and email code is 123456, which makes test setup quick.
HashKey's own symbols run together, like ``BTCUSDT`` for spot and ``BTCUSDT-PERPETUAL`` for futures. In LumiBot use the CCXT forms ``BTC/USDT`` and ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
A key made on the main trading account works with the main account first. For example, cancel all orders on a main account key does not cancel orders in sub trading accounts.
sources: HashKey Global API docs: Test our sandbox
HashKey Global API docs: Getting Started (sandbox and production URLs)
HashKey API Reference (new docs site: API key permissions, symbols)
HashKey Global Support: Important notes for submitting identity verification documents

hibachi.summary: Hibachi is a privacy-first exchange for leveraged perpetual contracts on crypto (and some FX pairs), such as BTC/USDT-P. You can sign up with a crypto wallet or with an email address.
signup_steps: Go to the Hibachi website. Either click Connect Wallet and approve the connection in your wallet (MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet and others), or click Create Account, enter your email address and finish the 6-digit code and two-factor setup.
Deposit funds. Hibachi takes USDT or USDC on the networks its docs list (Arbitrum and Base, for example). Only send a supported asset on the matching network.
Wait for your first deposit to land. Hibachi does not create your Account ID until then, and the API needs that ID.
api_key_steps: Log in on the Hibachi website, click the gear button in the top right corner and choose API Keys.
Click Create API Key and pick the account the key is for. A key only works for that one account.
Give the key a name and set API Restrictions to read-write with the Trading permission (see below), then click Generate.
Save the API Key and the Private Key right away. Hibachi shows the Private Key only once.
Click Next and note your Account ID, shown as ``ID: XXX`` under the key name.
hibachi.permissions: Choose read-write and turn on Trading, which Hibachi says is required to place orders. Leave Withdraws off (it lets a key send funds outside the exchange) and leave Transfers off unless you move money between your own sub-accounts. New keys start as read-only.
hibachi.testnet_note: Hibachi has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``HIBACHI_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Hibachi needs three values: ``HIBACHI_ACCOUNT_ID`` (the Account ID), ``HIBACHI_API_KEY`` and ``HIBACHI_PRIVATE_KEY``. In a code config these are ``"accountId"``, ``"apiKey"`` and ``"privateKey"``.

The Private Key from the API key page is not your crypto wallet's private key. Never use your wallet key here. Wallet (trustless) accounts get a key that signs with ECDSA, and email accounts get an HMAC secret; CCXT handles both.
CCXT's Hibachi adapter places limit orders only (no market orders), so give your orders a price.
Hibachi writes its perpetual markets like ``BTC/USDT-P``. In CCXT and LumiBot the same market is ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
sources: Hibachi API documentation: Getting Started and Key Definitions

hitbtc.summary: HitBTC is a crypto exchange with spot trading, margin trading (isolated and cross) and futures, including perpetual contracts. It offers REST and WebSocket APIs for automated trading.
signup_steps: Create a HitBTC account and open the link in the confirmation email.
Turn on two-factor authentication: in Settings, open the Security tab, click Add 2FA App, save the backup code and scan the QR code with an authenticator app.
For practice, HitBTC's API docs list a separate Demo Environment (Sandbox) at https://api.demo.hitbtc.com.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the API settings page in your account.
Click New API key. The new key starts with no access rights.
Copy the secret key right away. HitBTC hides it once you leave or reload the page.
Tick the access rights the bot needs (see below).
Confirm the change by email and with your 2FA code. HitBTC asks for both when you grant order or withdrawal rights.
hitbtc.permissions: Turn on Orderbook, History, Trading balance (to read balances, orders and trades) and Place/cancel orders (to trade). Leave the withdrawal right off, and skip Allow all. HitBTC notes that API actions such as withdrawals need only the API and secret keys, with no extra 2FA check.
hitbtc.testnet_note: HitBTC's API docs list a Demo Environment (Sandbox) at https://api.demo.hitbtc.com. Set ``HITBTC_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: You can make several API keys with different access rights. A separate key per bot keeps them apart and makes it easy to remove one.
HitBTC's own symbols look like ``BTCUSDT`` for spot and ``BTCUSDT_PERP`` for perpetuals. In LumiBot use the CCXT form: ``BTC/USDT`` for spot and ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the perpetual.
HitBTC supports sub-accounts with their own access settings, managed through the Subaccounts section of the API.
When you set up 2FA, HitBTC shows a backup code. Write it down and store it safely before you continue.
sources: HitBTC Support: How to enable 2FA with a code-generating app
HitBTC Support: Sign up and login (same account as HitBTC.com)

hollaex.summary: HollaEx Pro (pro.hollaex.com) is the crypto exchange run by HollaEx, the company that also makes white-label exchange software. It offers spot trading, mostly against USDT.
signup_steps: Create an account on HollaEx Pro at https://pro.hollaex.com.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). HollaEx needs 2FA before it lets you make an API key.
HollaEx Pro has no working public test site, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to HollaEx Pro and open Security, then API Keys from the sidebar (https://pro.hollaex.com/security?apiKeys).
Click Generate Key and give the key a name.
Enter the security codes HollaEx asks for (the email code and your 2FA code).
Copy the secret right away. HollaEx hides it for good once you refresh the page.
Set the key's access (see below) and add your bot's IP address to the key's whitelist.
hollaex.permissions: Turn on Reading and Trading. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
hollaex.testnet_note: HollaEx Pro has no usable sandbox. CCXT lists ``api.sandbox.hollaex.com`` as a test URL, but HollaEx's API docs do not mention a sandbox and that address refused requests on 2026-10-23. Test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``HOLLAEX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: HollaEx Pro writes pairs in lower case with a dash, like ``btc-usdt``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/USDT``.
The CCXT ``hollaex`` id talks to HollaEx Pro at ``api.hollaex.com``. Other exchanges built on HollaEx software have their own API addresses and are not covered by this id.
HollaEx signs every private request with an expiry time. Keep your bot machine's clock in sync so requests do not expire early.
sources: HollaEx docs: API guide (creating user API keys)
HollaEx API health endpoint (shows api.hollaex.com serves pro.hollaex.com)

htx.summary: HTX (formerly Huobi) is a large crypto exchange where you can buy and trade Bitcoin, Ethereum and hundreds of other coins. Through its API it offers spot trading plus futures and perpetual swaps.
signup_steps: Create an HTX account on the HTX website.
Link Google Authenticator (GA) and your phone and email. HTX asks for SMS, email and GA codes when you create an API key.
HTX shut down its testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on the HTX website, click the account icon in the upper right and choose API Management.
Fill in the Note field (a name for the key). It is required.
Enter the IP address of the machine that runs your bot, choose the permissions (see below) and click Create.
Complete the SMS, email and Google Authenticator checks, then click Confirm.
Copy the Access Key and Secret Key from the pop-up. HTX shows the Secret Key only once. If you lose it, you must make a new key.
htx.permissions: HTX keys have three permissions: Read, Trade and Withdraw. Turn on Read and Trade for a trading bot. Leave Withdraw off, a bot never needs to move money out of your account. One HTX key works for spot, futures, swaps and options.
htx.testnet_note: HTX shut down its testnet, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``HTX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bind an IP address to your key. HTX says a key with no IP binding expires after 90 days. A key can hold up to 20 IP addresses.

HTX sub-accounts keep assets and trades apart, and each one can have its own API keys with read and trade permissions. Create them on the website under Sub-Account Management. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
HTX's API still uses its old Huobi hostnames, such as ``api.huobi.pro``. HTX also runs ``api-aws.huobi.pro``, which it says has lower delay for servers on AWS.
Spot symbols look like ``BTC/USDT``. USDT-margined perpetual swaps use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
sources: HTX Support: How to apply for API Trading? How to create an API Key?
HTX Spot API documentation (Access and Authentication, Testnet, FAQ)
HTX Support: How to Create an HTX Sub-Account
HTX Support: FAQs on Linking 2FA to Your HTX Account

hyperliquid.summary: Hyperliquid is a fully onchain, non-custodial exchange that runs on its own blockchain. It offers more than 300 perpetual and spot markets, trading 24/7.
signup_steps: There is no account form. Open app.hyperliquid.xyz and click Connect, then log in with your email (you get a 6 digit code) or connect an EVM wallet such as Rabby or MetaMask.
If you use a wallet, click Enable Trading and sign the gas-less message. Then click Deposit and add USDC (for example USDC on Arbitrum).
For practice, use the testnet at app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz. Its faucet (https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/drip) gives 1,000 mock USDC to addresses that have already deposited on mainnet.
api_key_steps: Hyperliquid has no API key and secret. A bot signs with an API wallet (Hyperliquid's docs also call it an agent wallet).
Connect your main wallet on app.hyperliquid.xyz and open the API page (https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/API).
Type a name for the API wallet and click Generate. Save the private key it shows right away. It cannot be recovered later.
Click Authorize API Wallet and sign with your main wallet. Pick how long it stays valid (up to 180 days).
Give LumiBot the API wallet private key as ``privateKey`` and your main account address (not the API wallet address) as ``walletAddress``.
hyperliquid.permissions: There are no permission boxes to set. Hyperliquid says API wallets can act for your account without withdrawal permissions, so the API wallet can trade but cannot withdraw. Keep your main wallet's private key or seed phrase out of LumiBot.
hyperliquid.testnet_note: Hyperliquid has a testnet at https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz with its API at https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz. Authorize a separate API wallet there. Set ``HYPERLIQUID_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. With email login, Privy gives you a different wallet address on testnet than on mainnet.
extra_notes: Account data is looked up by your main account address. Hyperliquid warns that using the API wallet address for queries gives an empty result, so ``walletAddress`` must be your main (or sub-account) address.

An account can have 1 unnamed and up to 3 named API wallets, plus 2 more named ones per sub-account. Approving a new unnamed API wallet replaces the old one, so give each bot its own named API wallet.

API wallets expire on the Valid Until date you chose. When it passes, the bot stops trading until you authorize a new API wallet. Hyperliquid suggests a fresh API wallet each time, not reusing an old address.
In CCXT, Hyperliquid perpetuals use symbols like ``BTC/USDC:USDC`` and spot uses ``BTC/USDC``.
sources: Hyperliquid Docs: Nonces and API wallets
Hyperliquid Docs: Exchange endpoint (Approve an API wallet)
Hyperliquid Docs: How to start trading

independentreserve.summary: Independent Reserve is a crypto exchange that has operated since 2013. You can buy and sell major coins such as Bitcoin and Ethereum with AUD, NZD, SGD or USD.
signup_steps: Create an account with a username, email and password, and choose a personal account. Enter the code Independent Reserve emails you.
Finish identity verification: your details, a phone code, a photo ID, a selfie check and proof of address. Allow about 24 hours for review.
Turn on two-factor authentication during sign-up. It is optional, but you should use it.
api_key_steps: Log in, click the profile icon in the top right and choose Settings.
Open the API keys tab and click Generate API key.
Pick the access type (see below).
Enter a description and your password, and add your bot's IP address to the whitelist.
Click Generate and confirm with the SMS code. Copy the API key and API secret.
independentreserve.permissions: Choose the Trade role. Independent Reserve also offers Read Only, Full Access and Restricted Withdrawals, and it asks you to pick the lowest level you need. Do not pick Full Access or Restricted Withdrawals: a bot never needs to move money out.
independentreserve.testnet_note: Independent Reserve has no sandbox, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``INDEPENDENTRESERVE_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Whitelist your bot's IP address. Independent Reserve rejects a whitelisted key used from any other IP.
Keys made without an IP whitelist are turned off automatically if they go unused for 6 months.
BTC trades against AUD, USD, NZD and SGD, for example ``BTC/AUD`` or ``BTC/USD``.
sources: Independent Reserve: How to create a personal account
Independent Reserve: How to generate an API key for Fireblocks

indodax.summary: INDODAX is a crypto exchange with spot markets priced in Indonesian rupiah (IDR) and some in USDT. Its Trade API lets you read your account, place and cancel spot orders, and (only if you allow it) withdraw.
signup_steps: Create an INDODAX account on the website and finish the identity verification INDODAX asks for.
Set up your SMS PIN or Auth PIN (authenticator). INDODAX asks for one of them when you activate a Trade API key.
INDODAX has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in on the INDODAX website (the Trade API is not in the mobile app), open the Menu and choose Trade API, or go to https://indodax.com/trade_api.
Pick the API version. CCXT, and so LumiBot, uses the original Trade API at indodax.com/tapi, so choose Trade API V1.
Fill in a label and choose the permissions (see below).
Read the Terms and Conditions, tick I agree, and enter your SMS PIN or Auth PIN.
Click Activate Trade API, then click the confirmation link INDODAX sends to your email.
Save the API Key and Secret Key that appear. INDODAX shows the Secret Key only once; if you lose it, you must make a new key.
indodax.permissions: Turn on View (Enable Reading) and Trade (Enable Spot Trading). View lets the bot read balances and orders, and Trade lets it create and cancel orders. Leave Deposit & Withdraw off. A trading bot never needs to move money out of your account.
indodax.testnet_note: INDODAX has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``INDODAX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Most INDODAX markets are priced in rupiah, so use ``IDR`` as your quote asset (for example ``BTC/IDR``). INDODAX also lists some USDT pairs such as ``BTC/USDT``.

IP Permission is only required when a key has withdrawal access. A read and trade key can be made without an IP list. If you do add withdrawal access, the IP list then applies to every request made with that key.
The INDODAX trade endpoint allows about 20 requests per second per account and pair. Going over blocks trading on that pair for 5 seconds, so keep your bot's order rate modest.
INDODAX's official API docs are on GitHub at https://github.com/btcid/indodax-official-api-docs.
sources: INDODAX Help Center: How to Integrate the INDODAX API?
INDODAX Help Center: Is the Trade API feature available on the Indodax App?
INDODAX Help Center: What needs to be considered in the Trade API activation process?
INDODAX official API docs: Private REST API

kraken.summary: Kraken is a crypto exchange. Its Kraken Pro platform offers spot, margin and derivatives trading on more than 400 assets. LumiBot uses Kraken's spot API.
signup_steps: Create a Kraken account (or a Kraken Pro account at https://pro.kraken.com) with your email, a username and a strong password, then open the activation email and enter the activation key.
Finish verification. Kraken asks for your name, date of birth, phone number, address, occupation and a valid ID.
Turn on sign-in two-factor authentication in your Security settings. Kraken recommends a passkey, and an authenticator app also works.
api_key_steps: Sign in to Kraken Pro, open the account menu (the profile icon in the top right) and choose Settings.
Open the API tab and click Create API key.
Give the key a unique name, for example "LumiBot Trading Key".
Turn on the permissions listed below. You can also add IP whitelisting so the key only works from your bot's IP address.
Click Generate key.
Save the API key and the Private key in a password manager. Kraken says to treat them like your username and password.
kraken.permissions: Turn on Query Funds, Query Open Orders & Trades, Query Closed Orders & Trades, Modify Orders and Cancel/Close Orders. Access WebSockets API is also safe to turn on. Leave Withdraw Funds off. Kraken's own example says a trading key almost certainly does not need it, and a bot never needs to move money out of your account.
kraken.testnet_note: Kraken has no spot sandbox, and LumiBot's Kraken path has no sandbox switch, so test with a very small amount. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: With environment variables, LumiBot reads ``KRAKEN_API_KEY`` and ``KRAKEN_API_SECRET``. Kraken calls the secret the Private key.

Do not add two-factor authentication to the API key itself. Kraken explains that key 2FA only works if the software sends the 2FA code with every call, and LumiBot (through CCXT) does not send it, so every private call would fail.
Kraken lets you set a Key Expiration date. If you use one, plan to make a new key before it runs out, or your bot will stop logging in.
This page covers Kraken spot. Kraken futures is a separate exchange in CCXT with its own id, ``krakenfutures``, and its own keys.
sources: Kraken Support: How to create a spot API key
Kraken Support: How to create an account on Kraken Pro
Kraken Support: How to secure your account with two-factor authentication (2FA)

krakenfutures.summary: Kraken Futures (Kraken Derivatives) is Kraken's derivatives platform for perpetual futures and dated futures on crypto. It has its own REST, WebSocket and FIX APIs, separate from Kraken's spot API.
signup_steps: Create a Kraken account at https://www.kraken.com/sign-up.
Get fully verified (https://www.kraken.com/u/verify). Kraken requires full verification for personal accounts before you can unlock derivatives trading.

Unlock derivatives trading on your account, then sign in to your Kraken Derivatives account (https://www.kraken.com/login-futures). Kraken Futures has no working testnet right now, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Sign in to your Kraken Derivatives account.
Click your name in the upper-right corner and select Settings.
In the API panel, select the Create Key tab.
Set General API to Full Access and Withdrawal API to No Access (see below).
Press Create Key.
Save the public key and private key right away. Kraken shows the private key only once.
krakenfutures.permissions: Kraken Futures has two settings. Set General API to Full Access: it lets the bot read your account and place and cancel orders, and Kraken says it never includes withdrawals. Read Only cannot place orders. Set Withdrawal API to No Access. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
krakenfutures.testnet_note: Kraken has said its old Futures demo site (demo-futures.kraken.com) is decommissioned, and on 2026-10-23 that address only redirects to Kraken's main website. CCXT still lists it as the test URL, but it no longer works, so treat Kraken Futures as having no sandbox and test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``KRAKENFUTURES_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Kraken Futures has no spot markets. Use perpetual symbols in the full CCXT form: ``BTC/USD:USD`` is the USD-settled perpetual (Kraken's ``PF_XBTUSD``) and ``BTC/USD:BTC`` is the inverse perpetual settled in BTC (``PI_XBTUSD``). Kraken writes bitcoin as ``XBT``; CCXT converts it to ``BTC`` for you.
Kraken Futures keys do not work for Kraken spot trading, and spot keys do not work here. For Kraken spot, use the separate ``kraken`` CCXT id and a spot API key.

Kraken Derivatives sub-accounts each have their own API keys, rate limits and margin. Kraken links them on request through a support ticket, and withdrawals from sub-accounts are blocked, which suits a bot account.
You can create up to 50 API keys per account, and each has its own nonce. Give each bot its own key.
sources: Kraken Support: How to create an API key for Kraken Derivatives
Kraken Support: Kraken Derivatives eligibility requirements

kucoin.summary: KuCoin is a large crypto exchange. It offers spot trading, margin trading and futures, along with trading bots, copy trading and Earn products.
signup_steps: Sign up on the KuCoin site with your email or phone number, enter the code KuCoin sends you, and set a password.
Finish identity verification (KYC). KuCoin says new users must do this before using its products.
Set up Google 2FA and a trading password under Account Security. KuCoin asks for both, plus an email code, when you create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in at www.kucoin.com, click your avatar and choose API Management, then Create API.
In the window that opens, choose API Trading (not Link Third-Party Applications).
Enter an API name and an API passphrase. Write the passphrase down: LumiBot needs it, and KuCoin cannot recover it.
Pick the permissions (see below) and add the IP address of your bot to the whitelist.
Pass the security check with your trading password, email code and Google code, then confirm.
Save the API key, secret and passphrase right away. If you lose any of them you must make a new key.
kucoin.permissions: Turn on General (read-only: balances, statements and orders) and Spot (place and cancel spot orders). Add Futures only if your bot trades futures. Leave Withdrawal and Transfer off: Transfer lets the API move money without email or Google checks, and a bot never needs to move money out of your account.
kucoin.testnet_note: KuCoin has no sandbox in CCXT (no test URL listed), so test with a very small amount. Leave ``KUCOIN_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: KuCoin keys need three values: the API key, the secret and the passphrase you chose. Set ``KUCOIN_API_KEY``, ``KUCOIN_API_SECRET`` and ``KUCOIN_API_PASSPHRASE``.
Add an IP whitelist. KuCoin says keys with spot, margin or futures trading turned on but no IP address will be deleted or lose their trade permissions after 30 days of inactivity.
Sub-accounts can be created from the Sub-Account tab with Spot, Margin or Futures trading permissions. A sub-account per bot keeps bot funds and trades apart from manual trading.
Spot symbols look like ``BTC/USDT``. CCXT also has a separate ``kucoinfutures`` id for KuCoin futures, which has its own setup.
sources: KuCoin Help Center: How to Create API
KuCoin API docs: Introduction (API key permissions)
KuCoin Help Center: Sign Up and Login Help Guide for New Users
KuCoin Help Center: About Identity Verification
KuCoin Help Center: KuCoin Sub-Account Functions

kucoinfutures.summary: KuCoin Futures is the futures side of the KuCoin crypto exchange. It offers perpetual contracts that are USDT-margined or coin-margined (settled in the coin itself, like BTC).
signup_steps: Create a KuCoin account on the website and finish identity verification.
Turn on Google two-factor authentication and set a trading password. KuCoin asks for your trading password, an email code and a Google code when you create an API key.
KuCoin Futures has no testnet in CCXT, so plan to start with a very small live position.
api_key_steps: Log in, click your avatar and open API Management.
Click Create API and pick API Trading (not Link Third-Party Applications).
Enter an API name and make up a passphrase. Save the passphrase, because KuCoin cannot recover it.
Turn on the permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address to the whitelist.
Finish the security check with your trading password, email code and Google code.
Copy the API key and secret right away and store them with the passphrase.
kucoinfutures.permissions: Turn on General (read access) and Futures (futures trading). Leave withdrawals off. KuCoin says you must add an IP address to the whitelist before you can turn on the trading permissions.
kucoinfutures.testnet_note: KuCoin Futures has no sandbox in CCXT. Test with a very small position first, leave ``KUCOINFUTURES_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: CCXT has two KuCoin ids. Use ``kucoinfutures`` for perpetual futures like ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` and ``kucoin`` for spot like ``BTC/USDT``. Keys for both come from the same KuCoin API Management page; turn on the permission for what you trade.
Every KuCoin key needs three values: API key, secret and passphrase. Put the passphrase in ``KUCOINFUTURES_API_PASSPHRASE`` (or ``"password"`` in a code config).
Add an IP whitelist. KuCoin's help center says trading keys with no IP address can be deleted, or lose trading permission, after 30 days without use. Keys with only General permission do not expire.
KuCoin says coin-margined contracts such as ``BTC/USD:BTC`` are settled in their own coin (BTC here), while USDT-margined contracts like ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` are settled in USDT.
sources: KuCoin Support: How to Create API
KuCoin API docs: Get Apikey Info (permission names)

latoken.summary: LATOKEN is a crypto exchange that focuses on listing new tokens. It offers spot trading on hundreds of crypto pairs, plus an instant swap and token sales.
signup_steps: Click Sign up on https://latoken.com, enter your email and a password, and confirm your email with the 6-digit code LATOKEN sends you.
Turn on two-factor authentication under Profile, then the Security tab (Google Authenticator or SMS).
Identity verification (KYC) is only needed if you want API keys that can transfer or withdraw funds. A trading bot does not need those.
api_key_steps: Stay logged in for at least 24 hours without a break. LATOKEN only lets you create API keys after that, and a disconnect restarts the timer.
Click Profile in the top-right corner and select API Keys (https://latoken.com/account/apikeys/create-apikey).
Click Create API Key and enter a label you will recognize.
Choose the Trading on Spot permission set (see below) and click Create API Key.
Save the Public Key and Private Key right away. LATOKEN will not show them again.
latoken.permissions: Choose the Trading on Spot permission set. It can view your account and market data and place and cancel orders (PLACE_ORDER, CANCEL_ORDER), but it cannot move funds. Do not pick the sets that add transfers, withdrawals (WITHDRAW_WALLET) or BYPASS_2FA. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
latoken.testnet_note: LATOKEN has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``LATOKEN_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: LATOKEN splits your money into a Wallet account (deposits and withdrawals) and a Spot account (trading). The bot can only trade coins in the Spot account, so move funds from Wallet to Spot first, or turn on Auto-transfer in settings.
The Trading on Spot set keeps the bot limited to your Spot balance. Coins left in your Wallet account stay out of its reach.
To revoke a key, click the x in the top-right corner of its box on the API Keys page. This deletes the key for good.

LATOKEN Help Center: API Permissions Sets
LATOKEN Help Center: Spot & Wallet Accounts

LATOKEN Help Center: How to Enable 2FA
LATOKEN Help Center: What is LATOKEN?
LATOKEN Help Center: How to Buy & Sell on LATOKEN? (BTC/USDT example)

lbank.summary: LBank is a crypto exchange with a large list of spot markets, plus futures, spot margin, leveraged tokens and earn products.
signup_steps: Create an LBank account on the website or in the app.
Complete ID verification using the identity verification guide in LBank's support center.
Set up a security verification method (such as email codes or an authenticator app). LBank asks for it when you create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in on the LBank website and choose Profile, then My API (https://www.lbank.com/my/api-management).
Click Create New API.
Enter an API name, choose a verification method and enter your bot's IP address.
Choose the API purpose (see below) and click Confirm.
Finish the security verification and click Confirm. Copy the Secret Key right away; LBank shows it only once.
lbank.permissions: Choose Read Only and Trade. Add Futures only if your bot trades LBank perpetuals. Leave Withdraw and Transfer off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
lbank.testnet_note: LBank has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``LBANK_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bind an IP address to your key. LBank says trading keys with no IP bound expire after 30 days. You can bind up to 4 IP addresses to a trading key.
LBank writes pairs in lower case with an underscore, like ``btc_usdt``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/USDT``. Perpetuals use the full CCXT form, like ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
LBank supports both HmacSHA256 and RSA signatures. The standard key and secret from the steps above work with CCXT.
sources: LBank Support: How to Create and Manage Your API? (Web)
LBank Support: How to Create and Manage API (APP)

lighter.summary: Lighter is a decentralized exchange on an Ethereum layer 2 for trading perpetuals at low cost and low latency. It also lists some spot markets. Your Ethereum wallet owns your Lighter account.
signup_steps: Open the Lighter web app at https://app.lighter.xyz and connect your Ethereum wallet.
Make your first deposit (USDC for perpetuals). Lighter creates your account automatically on the first credited deposit.
For practice, use the Lighter testnet web app at https://testnet.app.lighter.xyz. It has its own accounts and its own server address.
api_key_steps: Use a separate Ethereum wallet just for your bot, and keep only bot money on its Lighter account (see below for why).

Find your account index: Lighter's number for your account. Each sub-account has its own index. CCXT looks up your main account index for you; set ``accountIndex`` in the CCXT options to use a sub-account.
Give LumiBot (through CCXT) your wallet's private key as ``privateKey``. CCXT uses it once to create and register a Lighter API key for you (registering a key needs a wallet signature).
CCXT uses API key index 254 by default. Indexes 0 to 3 belong to Lighter's own web and mobile apps, so if you set ``apiKeyIndex`` yourself, pick a number from 4 to 254.
CCXT also needs Lighter's signing library on your machine. Download it from Lighter's lighter-python repository (the signers folder) and set its path as the CCXT option ``libraryPath``.
lighter.permissions: Lighter API keys can trade, cancel, change leverage and make secure withdrawals, which can only go back to the wallet that owns the account. Sending money to other addresses also needs a wallet signature. CCXT asks for your wallet's private key, which can do everything, including those transfers. So use a separate wallet only for the bot, keep only bot money there, and never reuse your main wallet's key.
lighter.testnet_note: Lighter runs a testnet with its own web app at https://testnet.app.lighter.xyz and server at https://testnet.zklighter.elliot.ai. Set ``LIGHTER_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: CCXT signs Lighter orders with Lighter's signing library. Download it from Lighter's official Python SDK (https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python, folder lighter/signers) and pass its path as the CCXT option ``libraryPath`` in a code config, for example ``"options": {"libraryPath": "/path/to/signer"}``.
BTC trades only as a perpetual on Lighter (``BTC/USDC:USDC``). Spot markets are fewer, for example ``ETH/USDC``, which is why the spot example here uses ETH.
Each Lighter API key has its own order queue. Lighter suggests a separate API key for each independent workload, so if you run more than one bot, give each one its own ``apiKeyIndex``.
By default CCXT asks Lighter to approve an integrator fee for the CCXT project when it first connects. Set the CCXT option ``builderFee`` to ``False`` if you do not want that.
Lighter on Robinhood Chain is a separate exchange with its own servers. The CCXT id ``lighter`` connects to the main Lighter exchange.
sources: Lighter API Docs: Deposits, Transfers and Withdrawals
CCXT FAQ: How to use the Lighter Exchange in CCXT?
CCXT Lighter adapter source (libraryPath, apiKeyIndex and builderFee options)

luno.summary: Luno is a crypto exchange and app where you can buy, sell, store, send and receive Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. LumiBot uses it for spot trading against local currencies and stablecoins such as USDT and USDC.
signup_steps: Go to www.luno.com and select CREATE ACCOUNT (or use the Luno app), enter your email and a strong password, then confirm your email from the link Luno sends.
Verify your identity: select your initials, then Settings, then Verification, and follow the prompts. You confirm your details and give identity documents or a live selfie.
Keep your sign-in secure. Luno asks you to authorise high-risk actions, such as creating an API key, by push notification or email.
api_key_steps: Use the Luno website, not the app. Sign in, select your initials in the top left corner to open your profile, then Security.
From the Security menu choose API keys, then select CREATE API KEY.
Name the key and choose its permissions (see below). Tick Restrict IP address and enter your bot's IP address, then select NEXT.
Copy the API key ID and secret and save them. This is your only chance to see the secret.
Select CREATE API KEY, then approve the push notification or email Luno sends you.
luno.permissions: Pick Custom and turn on only View balance, View transactions, View orders and Create orders. Leave Send to any address and Create withdrawals off. Luno's help centre says its preset Trading access also lets an app send crypto out of your wallets and withdraw to a bank account, so a custom key is safer for a bot.
luno.testnet_note: Luno has no sandbox or testnet. Test with a very small amount on your real account, leave ``LUNO_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Luno's own API calls Bitcoin ``XBT`` (for example the pair ``XBTZAR``). CCXT maps it to ``BTC``, so in LumiBot write ``BTC/USDT`` or ``BTC/ZAR``.
Which pairs you can trade depends on your Luno account, from fiat pairs such as ``BTC/GBP``, ``BTC/ZAR`` or ``BTC/MYR`` to ``BTC/USDT`` and ``BTC/USDC``. Use a pair your account can trade.
You can also set an expiry date on the key. If you do, the bot stops working on that date until you make a new key.
When creating the key, stay on one device (or devices on the same router) and turn off any VPN. Luno says the setup can fail otherwise.

Luno Help Centre: How do I sign up for a Luno account?

mercado.summary: Mercado Bitcoin (MB) is a crypto exchange. It offers an API for buying, selling and checking orders, with prices in reais (BRL).
signup_steps: Create a Mercado Bitcoin account and verify it under Configurações > Cadastro.
Turn on two-step verification with an authenticator app (Configurações > Verificação em duas etapas > Aplicativo autenticador).
Turn on Dispositivo Seguro (secure device) in the MB app and send the selfie it asks for. MB needs all three before you can make an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in on the website, click your name in the top right and open Configurações.
In the side menu, under Integrações, choose Chave de API.
Click Nova Chave and fill in the fields.
Confirm with your 2FA code.
Copy the secret right away. MB shows it only once.
mercado.permissions: MB's help page does not list the permission names. Its API docs show that read-only keys exist and cannot place orders, so make sure the key can trade. Leave any withdrawal option off. A bot never needs to move money out.
mercado.testnet_note: Mercado Bitcoin has no sandbox, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``MERCADO_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Business (PJ) accounts cannot make keys this way. MB asks business customers to contact support.
MB's API pairs look like ``BTC-BRL``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/BRL``.
MB's default API rate limit is 500 requests per minute, shared by public and private calls.
sources: MB Central de Ajuda: Gestão de chave de API
MB Central de Ajuda: API de Negociação

mexc.summary: MEXC is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading and futures. MEXC says its API supports more than 1,200 spot and futures pairs.
signup_steps: Create a MEXC account on the website.
Turn on two-factor authentication. Spot API trading does not need identity verification (KYC), but futures API trading does.
MEXC has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to MEXC, click the profile icon in the top-right corner and choose API Management.
Tick the permissions you need (see below) and add a note so you can tell your keys apart.
Link the IP address of the machine that runs your bot. A key with no IP address expires after 90 days.
Click Create and finish the security verification.
Copy the Access Key and Secret Key right away. MEXC shows the Secret Key only once.
mexc.permissions: Tick the read permissions for your account and orders, plus spot trading (and futures trading only if you trade futures, which needs KYC). Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
mexc.testnet_note: MEXC says its API connects straight to live trading and has no sandbox or test environment, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``MEXC_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Bind an IP address to your key. MEXC keys with no IP address stop working after 90 days. Starting 5 days before expiry you can extend a key by 90 days under My API Key, Action, Renew.
You can limit which trading pairs a key may trade under My API Key, Trading Pairs, Set. If you use this, include every pair your bot trades.
MEXC offers API Only sub-accounts that have no web or app login. One of these per bot keeps bot trades apart from your own.
Each MEXC account can have up to 30 API keys, and each key can be linked to up to 10 IP addresses.
sources: MEXC Futures API docs: integration guide
MEXC Sub-Account and API Key Setup Manual

mudrex.summary: Mudrex is a crypto platform for buying, selling and trading Bitcoin and hundreds of other assets, plus crypto futures. Its trading API is for futures (perpetual contracts quoted in USDT).
signup_steps: Create an account on Mudrex at https://mudrex.com/ or in the Mudrex app.
Finish identity verification (KYC). Mudrex requires PAN and Aadhaar verification through DigiLocker before you can use the API.
Turn on TOTP two-factor authentication (an authenticator app). Mudrex needs it to create, rotate or revoke API keys. Mudrex has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to Mudrex and go to API key generation. Mudrex's API page (https://mudrex.com/pro-trading) has a Generate API Key button.
Give the key a clear name and click Generate Key. Mudrex currently allows one API key per user.
Copy both the API key and the API secret and store them safely. Mudrex shows the secret only once.
The secret is what signs every request. In CCXT, Mudrex only needs the ``secret`` value.
If the secret ever leaks, use Rotate in API Key Management to get a new secret (the old one stops working at once), or Revoke to shut the key off for good.
mudrex.permissions: Mudrex's docs do not offer permission choices when you create a key. A key can trade futures, manage positions and move funds between your own spot and futures wallets, and the API docs list no endpoint for withdrawing crypto out of Mudrex. Keep withdrawals in the app, and treat the API secret like a password.
mudrex.testnet_note: Mudrex has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``MUDREX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Mudrex's API covers futures only, so use the CCXT perpetual form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` (Mudrex calls it ``BTCUSDT``). Before trading, move funds from your spot wallet to your futures wallet; the API can do that transfer.

Mudrex futures can use USDT or INR as margin on the same USDT-priced contracts. USDT is the default. Leverage is stored separately for each currency, and the API cannot convert INR to USDT; do that in the Mudrex app.
Because there is only one API key per user, run one bot per Mudrex account, or make sure your bots share the key's rate limits (10 requests per second and 500 per minute on trading endpoints).
CCXT cannot load Mudrex markets without the API secret, so set the secret before starting the bot, even for data checks.
sources: Mudrex API docs: Authentication & Rate Limits
Mudrex API docs: API Key Management

myokx.summary: MyOKX is the OKX exchange site at my.okx.com. It offers spot trading and Convert, using the OKX v5 API served from the eea.okx.com host.
signup_steps: Register an OKX account on my.okx.com with your email, phone number, or an Apple or Google account.
Complete identity verification (KYC). OKX says it usually takes a few minutes to submit and up to 24 hours to finish.
For practice, open Trade, then Demo Trading. Your normal OKX login works there, and demo API keys are made separately from real ones.
api_key_steps: Log in on my.okx.com and open the API page from your profile (https://my.okx.com/account/my-api).
Click Create API key and pick the account it is for (your main account or a sub-account).
Enter a name and a passphrase, and add the IP address of your bot (up to 20 per key).
Under Permissions, choose Read and Trade.
Save the API key, secret key and passphrase. OKX cannot recover the passphrase, so a lost one means making a new key.
myokx.permissions: Turn on Read (view balances and order history) and Trade (place and cancel orders). Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
myokx.testnet_note: OKX runs Demo Trading for the API, using your normal OKX login. Create a separate key under Trade, Demo Trading, Personal Center, Demo Trading API. Demo keys only work in Demo Trading. Set ``MYOKX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to send LumiBot requests there. CCXT then adds OKX's demo trading header on the same eea.okx.com host.
extra_notes: MyOKX keys need three values: the API key, the secret key and the passphrase. Set ``MYOKX_API_KEY``, ``MYOKX_API_SECRET`` and ``MYOKX_API_PASSPHRASE``.
Bind an IP address to the key. OKX says keys with trade or withdraw permission and no bound IP expire after 14 days of inactivity (demo keys are not deleted).
Use the ``myokx`` id for accounts on my.okx.com. The ``okx`` id talks to the main okx.com API host instead, so a my.okx.com key belongs with ``myokx``.
Spot symbols look like ``BTC/EUR``. MyOKX also lists ``BTC/USDC`` and ``BTC/USDT``.
sources: MyOKX API docs (v5) overview, API key creation, permissions and demo trading
MyOKX Help: How can I do spot trading with the Jupyter Notebook? (creating API keys)

ndax.summary: NDAX is a crypto trading platform with a website and mobile app. Its public API lets you get market data, manage your account and place trades.
signup_steps: Click SIGN UP on the NDAX website or app. Enter your name, a username, email and password, then confirm the email link.
Verify your phone number with the 6 digit code NDAX sends.
Upload a government-issued ID and take the 3D selfie. NDAX says the review takes 0 to 2 business days.
api_key_steps: Log in to your NDAX account on the website or mobile app.
Click your profile icon (top right) and select API Keys.
Click Create New API Key.
Name the key and select the permissions (see below), then click Create.
Copy the API key and secret key from the popup and store them safely.
ndax.permissions: Select only the permissions the bot needs to read your account and trade. Leave any withdraw permission off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
ndax.testnet_note: NDAX's own help pages do not describe a public test environment. CCXT lists a staging address for NDAX, but NDAX does not document it for customers, so treat NDAX as having no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``NDAX_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: NDAX needs five credentials in CCXT: the API key, the secret, your numeric NDAX user ID, and your NDAX login username and password. Set ``NDAX_API_KEY``, ``NDAX_API_SECRET``, ``NDAX_UID``, ``NDAX_LOGIN`` and ``NDAX_API_PASSPHRASE`` (your login password). In a code config these are ``apiKey``, ``secret``, ``uid``, ``login`` and ``password``.
NDAX's API FAQ says the username and password must match the ones you use to log in to NDAX, and that the key and secret are case sensitive. Check these first if you see an invalid API key error.
NDAX's help center points developers to CCXT as its official integration files for Python, JavaScript and PHP.
Delete keys you no longer use under Settings, API Key, using the trash icon. A deleted key cannot be brought back.
