okx.summary: OKX is a large crypto exchange where you can buy and sell more than 300 coins. It also offers futures, options and other derivatives, plus trading bots and a crypto wallet.
signup_steps: Create an OKX account on the website or app.
Finish identity verification and turn on two-factor authentication.
For practice, open Trade, then Demo Trading. Demo trading uses its own API keys, made inside demo mode.
api_key_steps: Log in, open your Profile and go to API (API and connections). Click Create API key.
Enter a name for the key and pick the account (main account or a sub-account) it should use.
Add your bot's IP address to the IP allowlist. Each key can hold up to 20 addresses.
Pick the permissions (see below).
Make up a passphrase and type it in. OKX cannot show or recover it later, so save it.
Confirm with your two-factor code, then copy the API key and Secret key.
okx.permissions: Turn on Read and Trade. Leave Withdraw off. OKX says Trade covers placing and canceling orders, and it tells users never to turn on withdrawal for a trading tool.
okx.testnet_note: OKX does not have a separate testnet website. It has Demo Trading inside the normal OKX site. Make a demo key at Trade, then Demo Trading, then Personal Center, then Demo Trading API. Set ``OKX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) and use that demo key. Real keys do not work in demo mode, and demo keys do not work for real trading.
extra_notes: OKX keys have three parts: API key, Secret key and passphrase. Put the passphrase in ``OKX_API_PASSPHRASE`` (or ``"password"`` in a code config).
Always bind an IP address. OKX deletes a key that has Trade or Withdraw permission and no IP binding after 14 days without use.

OKX uses different API hosts for some sites. Accounts registered on app.okx.com use ``us.okx.com``, and accounts registered on my.okx.com use ``eea.okx.com``. CCXT has the ids ``okxus`` and ``myokx`` for those sites. Use ``okx`` for accounts on www.okx.com.
Make the key inside the sub-account you want the bot to use. OKX says not to mix the main account's and a sub-account's key, secret or passphrase.
sources: OKX API v5 docs: overview, API key creation, demo trading and API domains
OKX Help: How do I connect a third-party trading terminal or bot to my OKX account?

okxus.summary: OKX US is the OKX exchange for accounts registered on app.okx.com. It uses the same OKX v5 API as OKX, but through its own API host, us.okx.com.
signup_steps: Create an OKX account at https://app.okx.com and complete the setup steps OKX shows you.
Fund your account. OKX may require more than 100 USD in the account before it lets you create an API key.
For practice, open Trade, then Demo Trading, to get a demo account. Demo keys are made separately (see the sandbox note).
api_key_steps: Log in, go to Profile and select API and connections, then click Create API key.
Enter a key name and choose the account and what the key is used for.
Add your bot's IP address to the IP allowlist (up to 20 addresses per key).
Pick the permissions (see below) and type a passphrase you make up yourself.
Save the API key, secret key and passphrase. OKX cannot recover a lost passphrase, so you would need a new key.
okxus.permissions: Turn on Read and Trade. Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account. OKX notes that Trade also covers funding transfers and settings, so keep the key private.
okxus.testnet_note: OKX US offers Demo Trading. Create a demo key under Trade, then Demo Trading, then Personal Center, then Demo Trading API. Demo requests go to the same us.okx.com host with a demo flag, and demo keys only work in demo. Set ``OKXUS_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: OKX needs three values: put the passphrase in ``OKXUS_API_PASSPHRASE`` next to ``OKXUS_API_KEY`` and ``OKXUS_API_SECRET``.

Pick the CCXT id that matches where you signed up: ``okxus`` for app.okx.com accounts (API host us.okx.com), ``myokx`` for my.okx.com accounts (API host eea.okx.com) and ``okx`` for other OKX accounts. OKX says the default openapi.okx.com host does not work for app.okx.com or my.okx.com accounts.
If a key has Trade permission but no IP allowlist, OKX lets it expire after 14 days without use. Add your bot's IP to avoid this. Demo keys do not expire this way.
OKX suggests one key per tool, so you can turn one off without touching the others. If a key may have leaked, delete it first, then make a new one.

onetrading.summary: One Trading (formerly Bitpanda Pro) is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading and futures, open 24/7.
signup_steps: Click Open Account on the One Trading site, fill in your details and log in with your new email and password.
Set up two-factor authentication. One Trading makes 2FA mandatory and it cannot be turned off.
Complete identity verification when One Trading asks for it.
api_key_steps: Log in, click your profile in the top right corner and open the API Keys tab.
Click New API key and give it a name.
Choose the permissions (see below). If you like, limit the key to up to five IP addresses.
Click Create API key and copy the key right away. This is the only time One Trading shows it.
Confirm the key with the link One Trading emails you. The link expires after 2 hours, so use the newest email.
onetrading.permissions: Choose Read and Trade. Read covers balances and market data; Trade lets the bot place and cancel orders. Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
onetrading.testnet_note: One Trading has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``ONETRADING_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, always set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Check that a market is open before you trade it. On 2026-10-23 One Trading's instruments list showed the BTC_EUR spot market as CLOSED, while BTC_USDC spot was ACTIVE, so this example uses ``BTC/USDC``.
If you used Bitpanda Pro before, log in to One Trading with your old Bitpanda Pro account. The CCXT id is ``onetrading``.
One Trading allows about 240 requests per minute. Too many requests return HTTP 429, so keep your bot's polling modest.
One Trading supports subaccounts. A key acts on one account (the main account or a subaccount), so a separate subaccount per bot keeps trades apart.

One Trading Support: How do I set up and reset Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?

p2b.summary: P2B (p2pb2b.com) is a centralized crypto exchange for buying and selling Bitcoin, Ether and a wide range of other tokens. LumiBot uses its spot markets.
signup_steps: Click Register on p2pb2b.com, enter your email and a password, agree to the Terms of Use and click Sign Up.
Open the confirmation email from P2B and click the link to verify your email address.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) in Account, Security (https://p2pb2b.com/account/security). P2B's API docs say to do this before you make an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in to P2B and make sure 2FA is on (Account, Security).
Open Account, API (https://p2pb2b.com/account/api).
Generate a new API key and secret.
Copy the API key and the API secret and keep them somewhere safe. LumiBot needs both.
p2b.permissions: P2B's API docs do not list permission settings for keys. The private API they describe only covers balances and trading (placing, cancelling and checking orders), with no withdrawal endpoint. If the key page offers a withdrawal option, leave it off. A trading bot never needs to move money out.
p2b.testnet_note: P2B has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``P2B_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: P2B's API only creates limit orders (every new order needs a price). Market orders are not supported, so use limit orders in your strategy.
Orders that break a market's limits (minimum amount, step size, tick size or minimum total) are not created. CCXT loads these limits for each market.
P2B allows at most 10 private API requests per second, and it rejects a repeated nonce within the same second. Avoid running two bots on one key at the same time.
BTC trades against USDT, USDC and USD on P2B, for example ``BTC/USDT``.
sources: P2B API documentation (GitHub, official P2B team)
P2B blog: How to Register on a Cryptocurrency Exchange?

pacifica.summary: Pacifica is a decentralized, self-custody trading platform on Solana that launched in June 2025. It offers perpetual futures on crypto and other markets, plus spot markets quoted in USDC. In CCXT, Pacifica is set up for its perpetual markets.
signup_steps: There is no account form. Open app.pacifica.fi and connect a Solana wallet such as Phantom, Solflare or Backpack.
Deposit USDC into your Pacifica account. Pacifica lists a 10 dollar minimum deposit.
Keep your main wallet's secret key or seed phrase private. The bot uses a separate agent key instead (see below).
api_key_steps: Pacifica has no API key and secret. A bot signs with an API Agent Key (Pacifica also calls it an agent wallet).
With your main wallet connected, open the API key page at https://app.pacifica.fi/apikey.
Generate an agent key and bind it to your account. You sign the binding in your browser, so your main secret never leaves your wallet.
Save the agent wallet's private key and its public key in a safe place.
Give LumiBot the agent private key as ``privateKey`` and your main account address as ``walletAddress``. CCXT reads the agent's public key from the ``agentAddress`` option.
pacifica.permissions: There are no permission boxes to set. Pacifica says an agent key can trade, but cannot move funds the way your main wallet can, and you can revoke it at any time. Keep your main wallet's private key out of LumiBot.
pacifica.testnet_note: Pacifica runs a testnet with its API at https://test-api.pacifica.fi, and it uses test USDC called USDP. Bind a separate agent key for the testnet. Set ``PACIFICA_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: CCXT needs your main account address as ``walletAddress`` (set ``PACIFICA_WALLET_ADDRESS``) and the agent key as ``privateKey``. If the agent key is not your main key, also set the CCXT option ``agentAddress`` to the agent wallet address in a code config, for example ``"options": {"agentAddress": "..."}``.
Requests always use your main account's public address as the account. The agent key only signs, so ``walletAddress`` must be your main (or sub-account) address, not the agent address.
Perpetuals use cross margin by default, with isolated margin available. Leverage ranges from 3x to 50x depending on the market.
Pacifica market symbols are case sensitive, for example ``BTC`` and ``kBONK``. In CCXT the BTC perpetual is ``BTC/USDC:USDC``.
Pacifica uses a credit-based rate limit with a 60-second rolling window, so keep the bot's polling modest.
sources: Pacifica Docs: MCP Configuration (agent key and testnet host)
CCXT Pacifica adapter source (credential and agentAddress options)

paradex.summary: Paradex is a trading venue that runs on its own appchain on Starknet. It says you can trade perps, options and spot from one account with zero fees.
signup_steps: Open https://app.paradex.trade and click Connect Wallet. Choose your Ethereum wallet, such as MetaMask.
Sign the request that creates your Paradex (L2) key. The first time, Paradex asks you to sign twice.
For practice, use the testnet at https://app.testnet.paradex.trade. It runs on Sepolia and credits each new account with $1,000,000 of test USDC.
api_key_steps: Make a new Ethereum wallet just for the bot, and connect it to Paradex as above.
Set ``PARADEX_WALLET_ADDRESS`` to that wallet's Ethereum address.
Set ``PARADEX_PRIVATE_KEY`` to that wallet's private key. CCXT signs with it to find your Paradex account and log in.
Fund only what the bot will trade.
Paradex also offers subkeys (Key Management, Subkeys, + Add New Key) that can trade but cannot withdraw. CCXT's Paradex login does not use the subkey flow, so they do not replace the key above.
paradex.permissions: Paradex subkeys can place, cancel and change orders but cannot withdraw or transfer. However, CCXT logs in with the wallet's private key, and that key has full control, including withdrawals. Use a separate wallet that holds only the bot's funds, and never reuse your main wallet's key.
paradex.testnet_note: Paradex runs a testnet at https://app.testnet.paradex.trade on Ethereum's Sepolia network, with free test USDC. Set ``PARADEX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. Testnet accounts cannot be reset; make a sub-account or a new wallet to get more test funds.
extra_notes: In CCXT, Paradex lists perpetuals (and options) but no spot markets. The BTC perpetual is ``BTC/USD:USDC``, settled in USDC.
Paradex login tokens (JWTs) expire every 5 minutes. CCXT gets new ones for you.
Paradex supports sub-accounts. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.

paymium.summary: Paymium is a crypto exchange with a wallet, trading in euros (for example BTC/EUR) and a payment gateway. It offers REST and WebSocket APIs for market data and automated trading.
signup_steps: Sign up with your email address and click the link Paymium emails you, then enter your details and the SMS code to confirm your phone.
Fill in the compliance form and finish identity verification (photo of your ID, a short face video and an e-signature), then upload a proof of address under Profile, Documents.
Wait for Paymium to review your documents (it says 24 to 48 working hours). Paymium has no testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to your Paymium account. Paymium says only fully verified and approved accounts can use the authenticated API.
Open the developer tokens page at https://account.paymium.com/developers/tokens. This is where the Create an API key button on Paymium's API page goes.
Create a new API token.
Copy the token (your API key, shown in the list of active tokens) and its secret, and store them safely.
paymium.permissions: Paymium's API docs list these access scopes: basic (account and balances), activity (orders, deposits and withdrawals history), trade (create and cancel orders) and withdraw. A trading bot needs basic, activity and trade. Leave withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
paymium.testnet_note: Paymium has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``PAYMIUM_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Paymium trades in euros. The main market in CCXT is ``BTC/EUR``, so use ``EUR`` as your quote asset.
Paymium's API docs say every signed request needs a nonce that is larger than the one before. Giving each bot its own token keeps two programs from sending nonces out of order.
CCXT waits about 2 seconds between Paymium requests to respect its rate limits, so expect slower updates than on larger exchanges.
sources: Paymium: Crypto API for trading, wallet and payments
Paymium Help: How to open an individual account on Paymium?

phemex.summary: Phemex is a crypto exchange founded in 2019 that offers spot trading and perpetual futures. Phemex says more than 10 million traders use it.
signup_steps: Create a Phemex account with an email address (or another sign-in method Phemex offers).
Finish identity verification (KYC) and turn on two-factor authentication.
For practice, also create a separate account on the Phemex testnet at https://testnet.phemex.com. Testnet keys only work on the testnet.
api_key_steps: Log in and open API Management from your account menu (https://phemex.com/account/api-management).
Click Create New API Key.
Choose Default API entry. The High Rate Limit entry is meant for heavy, professional use.
Enter a name and the IP address of the machine that will run your bot.
Pick the permission level, click Confirm and enter the email verification code.
Copy the key and secret right away. Phemex shows the key only once.
phemex.permissions: Use read and trade access. Leave withdrawals off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
phemex.testnet_note: Phemex runs a full testnet at https://testnet.phemex.com with its own accounts and keys. Set ``PHEMEX_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to send LumiBot requests there.
extra_notes: Phemex perpetual symbols use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` (settled in USDT) or ``BTC/USD:BTC`` (inverse, settled in BTC). Spot is plain ``BTC/USDT``.
Phemex also offers sub-accounts, and you can share one API key with sub-accounts from API Management. A separate sub-account per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
sources: Phemex Help Center: How do I create an API key?
Phemex Help Center: share API keys with sub-accounts

poloniex.summary: Poloniex is a crypto exchange. Its API covers spot trading and futures (perpetual contracts), and LumiBot uses the spot API.
signup_steps: Create a Poloniex account at https://www.poloniex.com/signup and confirm your email.
Finish any identity checks Poloniex asks for.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Poloniex asks for your 2FA code when you turn on the API and again when you create a key.
api_key_steps: Log in and open the spot API key page in your profile settings (https://www.poloniex.com/profile/settings/spot-api-key).
If the API is not on yet, click Enable API, enter your 2FA code and confirm with the email Poloniex sends. The email link expires in 15 minutes.
Click the button to create a new key and enter your 2FA code again.
Confirm the new key from the second email Poloniex sends.
Poloniex then shows your API key and secret. Copy both right away and keep them somewhere safe.
poloniex.permissions: The key needs to read your account and trade. Leave withdrawals off. Poloniex turns withdrawals off by default because API withdrawals skip 2FA and email checks, and a bot never needs to move money out of your account.
poloniex.testnet_note: Poloniex's current API docs do not describe a sandbox. CCXT still lists an old test URL for Poloniex, but that host did not answer on 2026-10-23, so test with a very small amount instead. With environment variables, leave ``POLONIEX_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Poloniex writes its own symbols as ``BTC_USDT``. In LumiBot and CCXT use the standard form, ``BTC/USDT``. CCXT also lists Poloniex perpetuals such as ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
IP access restriction is off by default. Poloniex says to turn it on only if your bot runs from a static IP address, because a changing IP would lock the key out.
Spot and futures use different keys. Spot keys come from the spot API key page, and futures keys come from https://www.poloniex.com/profile/settings/futures-api-key.

toobit.summary: Toobit is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading, USDT-M and USDC-M perpetual contracts, copy trading and P2P trading.
signup_steps: Sign up on the Toobit register page with your email or phone number, set a password, and enter the verification code Toobit sends you.
Turn on Google Authenticator: open Profile, then Security Settings, and click Settings next to Google Verification. Toobit asks for this code when you create an API key.
Optional: create a sub-account for your bot (profile icon, then Sub-account, then Create sub-account) and move funds to it with Transfer.
api_key_steps: On the Toobit website (keys cannot be made in the app), click the user icon at the top right and choose API Management (https://www.toobit.com/en-US/user/sub-api).
Click New API.
Name the key, set its permissions (see below) and add the IP address of your bot to the IP whitelist, then press Confirm.
Enter your Google Authenticator code and click OK.
Copy the Secret Key right away. Toobit shows it only once.
toobit.permissions: A new Toobit key can only read at first (Enable Reading). Turn on the trade permission so the bot can place and cancel orders. Leave any withdrawal permission off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
toobit.testnet_note: Toobit has a Demo Trading page on its website, but CCXT lists no test URL for Toobit, so LumiBot cannot point at it. Test with a very small amount, leave ``TOOBIT_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Toobit API keys expire 90 days after they are created. Put a reminder in your calendar to make a new key before then, or your bot will stop trading.
Each Toobit account can have at most 10 API keys. You can freeze, delete or change the permissions of a key from the API list.
Toobit's own symbols look like ``BTCUSDT``. In LumiBot use the CCXT form: spot is ``BTC/USDT`` and the USDT perpetual is ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
Sub-accounts keep their own funds and trading apart from the main account, which makes them a good home for a bot.

upbit.summary: Upbit is a spot crypto exchange. Its Open API covers market prices and candles, plus orders, balances, deposits and withdrawals for your own account.
signup_steps: Create an Upbit account.
Finish customer verification (identity check). Upbit only lets you make an API key after this step.
Turn on two-channel authentication (2FA). Upbit's global sites call this reaching security level 2.
api_key_steps: Log in on the Upbit PC website. API keys cannot be made in the app.
Go to My Page, then Open API Management (https://upbit.com/mypage/open_api_management).
Pick the permissions for the key (see below) and enter the public IP address of the machine that runs your bot. A fixed (static) IP works best.
Agree to the data notice and click the button to issue the Open API key.
Finish the two-channel authentication check.
Copy the Access Key and Secret Key. Upbit shows the Secret Key only once.
upbit.permissions: Turn on View Account (asset lookup), View Orders and Make Orders. Upbit asks for an allowlisted IP address when Make Orders is on. Leave Withdraw off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
upbit.testnet_note: Upbit has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``UPBIT_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Upbit needs only two credentials: the Access Key (``UPBIT_API_KEY``) and the Secret Key (``UPBIT_API_SECRET``). There is no passphrase.
Requests from an IP address that is not on the key's list fail with ``no_authorization_ip``. Private IP addresses cannot be added. Use the public IP of your server.
Upbit API keys can expire. The global docs say to delete an expired key from the Expired Keys tab, and an ``expired_access_key`` error means you need to issue a new key.

CCXT's ``upbit`` talks to api.upbit.com by default. Upbit's other sites use their own API hosts (sg-api.upbit.com, id-api.upbit.com, th-api.upbit.com), which CCXT reaches through its ``hostname`` option. Use the host for the site where you opened your account.

weex.summary: WEEX is a crypto exchange for spot trading and USDT-margined futures, with more than 100 coins. Its API covers both spot and futures trading.
signup_steps: Create a WEEX account on the website.
Set up your account security. WEEX asks you to pass a security verification when you create an API key.
WEEX has no testnet, so plan to start with a very small trade.
api_key_steps: Log in to WEEX on the website and go to Account, then API Management (https://www.weex.com/account/newapi).
Click Create API Key.
Make up a passphrase. WEEX cannot recover it, so save it. If you lose it you must make a new key.
Pick the permissions (see below). New keys start as Read Only.
Add your bot's IP address to the IP allowlist (up to 10 addresses, separated by commas).
Finish the security check, then copy the API key and secret key and store them with the passphrase.
weex.permissions: Keep read access and add the Spot trading permission so the bot can place spot orders. Leave any withdrawal setting off. New WEEX keys start as Read Only, so a key will not trade until you add the trading permission.
weex.testnet_note: WEEX has no sandbox. Test with a very small amount, leave ``WEEX_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: WEEX keys have three parts: API key, secret key and passphrase. Put them in ``WEEX_API_KEY``, ``WEEX_API_SECRET`` and ``WEEX_API_PASSPHRASE``.
Bind an IP address. WEEX warns that keys with no IP binding are a security risk.
Each WEEX user can have up to 10 API key groups, so you can give each bot its own key.
WEEX uses separate API hosts for spot and for contracts (futures). CCXT's WEEX setup uses ``api-spot.weex.com`` for spot, and WEEX's docs show ``api-contract.weex.com`` for contract data.

WEEX API page (spot and futures API, FAQ)

whitebit.summary: WhiteBIT is a centralized crypto exchange with 350+ trading pairs. It offers spot trading, margin trading and futures.
signup_steps: Create a WhiteBIT account on https://whitebit.com.
Pass identity verification (KYC). WhiteBIT needs it before you can make deposits or withdrawals.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). WhiteBIT requires 2FA before you can create API keys.
api_key_steps: Log in on the WhiteBIT website, open Settings and go to the API block, then API keys.
Click Generate API key and enter your 2FA code.
Name the key and, under endpoint access restrictions, turn on only the categories the bot needs (see below).
Click Confirm and enter your 2FA code again.
Save the Secret Key right away. WhiteBIT cannot show it again after you close the page. You can then add your bot's IP addresses to the trusted list.
whitebit.permissions: Turn on Trading Balance and History and Order Management. Leave Withdrawal, Deposit and Transfer between balances off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
whitebit.testnet_note: WhiteBIT has no sandbox, and CCXT lists no test URL for it, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``WHITEBIT_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Deposits land in your Main balance, but spot trades use your Trade balance (margin and futures use the Collateral balance). Move funds to the Trade balance on the website before you start the bot.
If you turn on the trusted IP list and a request comes from any other IP, WhiteBIT turns the key off and emails you. You can add up to 20 trusted IPs per key.
WhiteBIT turns off an API key after 14 days without use. You can see each key's expiry date under API keys, and reactivate it on the API settings page.
WhiteBIT offers free Demo Tokens, a practice asset on the live exchange, to try spot trading and test your API keys. They are not a separate test site, so LumiBot's sandbox setting does not apply.

woo.summary: WOO X is a crypto exchange with spot and futures markets. It also offers social (copy) trading and earn products.
signup_steps: Click the sign-up button on woox.io, enter your email and a password, then enter the code WOO X emails you within 10 minutes.
Complete identity verification (KYC) from the Account page with Level up.
Bind two-factor authentication (2FA). WOO X needs it before you can create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in to WOO X and open the Subaccount and API tab on the account page.
Click Create API.
Enter a description for the key, for example the name of your bot.
Choose the permissions (see below) and add your bot's IP address as a trusted IP.
Enter your 2FA code to confirm, then save the API key and secret. The secret is never shown again; if you lose it, delete the key and make a new one.
woo.permissions: Turn on Read and Enable Trading. Leave Enable Withdrawals off. WOO X itself advises against withdrawal permission on keys used for automated trading.
woo.testnet_note: WOO X documents a testnet (staging) site at https://staging.woox.io with its REST API at https://api.staging.woox.io. Set ``WOO_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it. WOO X presents the testnet as part of its institutional API setup, so you may need to ask WOO X support for access.
extra_notes: WOO X subaccounts can have their own API keys. A separate subaccount per bot keeps bot trades apart from manual trades.
WOO X moved its API from ``api.woo.org`` to ``api.woox.io``. If an old setup points at api.woo.org, update it to the new domain.
Perpetual futures use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT``. Spot is plain ``BTC/USDT``.
CCXT also has a ``woofipro`` id. That is WOOFi Pro, a separate on-chain exchange, not WOO X. Use ``woo`` for WOO X accounts.

woofipro.summary: WOOFi Pro is an order book exchange for perpetual futures, built on Orderly Network. You keep custody of your funds and trade with USDC.
signup_steps: Open WOOFi Pro and sign in with email, a social login, or a crypto wallet on a supported chain.
Sign the two free signature requests WOOFi Pro shows to enable trading (they cost no gas), then deposit USDC with the Deposit button.
For practice, open the WOOFi Pro testnet at https://testnet-pro.woofi.com/en/trade/ETH_PERP and click Get test USDC. Test funds show up after a few minutes.
api_key_steps: Log in to WOOFi Pro and open the API key page in your Portfolio (https://pro.woofi.com/en/portfolio/api-key).
Click Create API key.
Confirm the request. WOOFi Pro then shows your Account ID, Orderly Key and Orderly Secret.
Copy all three somewhere safe. In LumiBot (through CCXT), the Account ID is ``accountId``, the Orderly Key is ``apiKey`` and the Orderly Secret is ``secret``.
Note the key's expiry date. Orderly keys expire, at most 365 days after they are added, so make a new key before then.
woofipro.permissions: Orderly keys have two scopes: read (account data) and trading (placing and cancelling orders). Your bot needs both. Withdrawals cannot be done with the Orderly key alone: Orderly requires a signature from your wallet for every withdrawal, so the bot's key can trade but cannot move money out.
woofipro.testnet_note: WOOFi Pro has a testnet at https://testnet-pro.woofi.com with free test USDC from the Get test USDC button. Make a separate API key there. Set ``WOOFIPRO_SANDBOX=true`` (or ``"sandbox": True`` in a code config) to use it.
extra_notes: WOOFi Pro only lists perpetual futures, so symbols use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDC:USDC``. There are no spot markets.
WOOFi Pro's old address dex.woo.org now redirects to https://pro.woofi.com.
The CCXT id ``woofipro`` is WOOFi Pro. The CCXT id ``woo`` is the separate WOO X exchange, with its own accounts and keys.

Orderly Docs: Wallet Authentication (Orderly key scopes, expiry, withdrawals)

xt.summary: XT.COM is a crypto exchange that offers spot trading, futures, margin trading and copy trading. Its API covers spot and futures trading, among other services.
signup_steps: Visit www.xt.com, click Sign up and register with your email or phone number. Enter the 6-digit code XT.COM sends you.

Complete identity verification: go to Profile, then KYC Verification, click Verify Now and follow the steps (ID document photos and a live face check). XT.COM says review usually takes up to 2 business days.
Turn on Google Authenticator. You need its code to create an API key.
api_key_steps: Log in at www.xt.com and open API Management in the User Center.
Apply for API trading first: click Create API, then Submit for Review. XT.COM reviews the request for risk control, which can take 3 to 5 business days.
Once approved, go back to API Management, enter an Alias Name and your bot's IP address in Whitelist IP.
Enter your Google verification code and click Create API.
Copy the Public Key and Private Key (secret) right away. XT.COM shows them only once and cannot recover a lost secret.
Click Modify on the new key to turn on trading permission (see below).
xt.permissions: A new XT.COM key has query (read) permission only. Use Modify to turn on trading for the markets you trade. Leave withdrawal off. A bot never needs to move money out of your account.
xt.testnet_note: XT.COM has no sandbox or testnet. Test with a very small amount on your real account, leave ``XT_SANDBOX`` unset, and in a code config set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: API trading on XT.COM needs approval before your key can trade. XT.COM says a balance above 50,000 USDT speeds up the review, so apply early and wait for approval before starting the bot.
Each user can create up to 10 API keys. Sub-accounts (up to 20 per main account) can each have their own keys, which helps keep each bot's funds apart.
The spot REST API lives at https://sapi.xt.com. XT.COM advises against reaching the API through a proxy because of latency and stability problems.
In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/USDT`` for spot and ``BTC/USDT:USDT`` for the USDT perpetual.

XT Support: How to register on XT?

zaif.summary: Zaif is a crypto exchange. It offers an order book exchange, an easy buy and sell desk, coin accumulation plans and automated trading, with prices in yen.
signup_steps: Create an account with your email address and a strong password, in the Zaif app or browser.
Enter your details and finish identity verification as Zaif asks.
Set up two-step verification with an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator. Zaif requires it to log in and to manage API keys.
api_key_steps: Log in to Zaif.
Open the API key page (https://zaif.jp/api_keys) from your account information.
Create a new key and give it only the rights it needs (see below).
Register your bot's IP address under IP address restriction.
Confirm with your two-step code, then save the key and secret somewhere safe.
zaif.permissions: Give the key info and trade rights. Zaif asks you to keep key rights to the minimum and not to grant withdraw unless you really need it, so leave withdraw off. Zaif warns that an API key can trade without the login two-step check, so a leaked key can cause direct losses.
zaif.testnet_note: Zaif has no sandbox, so test with a very small amount. With environment variables, leave ``ZAIF_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: Zaif's API takes limit orders only. Every order needs a price, and Zaif says market orders by API are still under review. Use limit orders in your strategy.
Zaif's smallest BTC/JPY order is 0.001 BTC (its public API lists this as item_unit_min), so the example uses about 15,000 yen. Keep every BTC order at 0.001 BTC or more.
Zaif writes pairs like ``btc_jpy``. In LumiBot and CCXT use ``BTC/JPY``.
Delete keys you no longer use, and change or delete keys when someone with access leaves.

Zaif Support: recommended environment and security measures

zebpay.summary: ZebPay is a crypto exchange with spot markets, including crypto pairs priced in Indian rupees (INR), and perpetual futures. ZebPay says it has 40+ spot markets and 60+ futures markets that share one API sign-in system.
signup_steps: Create a ZebPay account and finish KYC verification. Your KYC status shows on the My Account page.
Make sure your mobile number and email are confirmed. ZebPay sends a 6-digit code to both when you create an API key.
ZebPay's own docs describe no public testnet, so plan to test with a very small amount.
api_key_steps: Log in to ZebPay in a web browser.
Go to API Trading from the navigation bar on the left and click Create New API Key.
Name your key and choose the permissions (see below).
Add your bot's IP address to the IP whitelist. It is optional, but it limits the key to your machine.
Enter the 6-digit code ZebPay sends to your mobile number and email.
Save the Secret Key right away. ZebPay shows it only once.
zebpay.permissions: ZebPay keys have Read, Trade and Withdraw permissions. Turn on Read and Trade. Leave Withdraw off. A trading bot never needs to move money out of your account.
zebpay.testnet_note: CCXT lists a ZebPay staging address (zebstage.com), but ZebPay's own API docs do not describe a public testnet or how to get keys for it. Test with a very small amount on the live exchange instead. With environment variables, leave ``ZEBPAY_SANDBOX`` unset. In a code config, set ``"sandbox": False``.
extra_notes: ZebPay spot markets include rupee pairs such as ``BTC/INR`` and USDT pairs such as ``BTC/USDT``. Perpetual futures use the full CCXT form, for example ``BTC/USDT:USDT``.
Spot and futures use different API hosts (sapi.zebpay.com for spot, futuresbe.zebpay.com for futures), but ZebPay says they share the same authentication framework. CCXT picks the right host for you.
You can see each key's rate limits and revoke a key at any time from My Account.
ZebPay's official API docs are on GitHub at https://github.com/zebpay/zebpay-api-references. ZebPay notes the spot docs are still being expanded.

ZebPay Help: Your ZebPay My Account

skipped.derive: Derive moved to its v3 API and the CCXT version LumiBot has installed (4.5.64, the version ccxt_exchange_facts.json was built from) still targets the old v2 host. Checked 2026-10-23: ccxt.derive().load_markets() fails with 503 Service Unavailable from https://api.lyra.finance/public, and the same host returns 503 directly. Derive's own docs (https://docs.derive.xyz/getting-started/introduction, https://docs.derive.xyz/migrating/breaking-changes) list the current endpoints as https://api.derive.xyz/v3 (mainnet, UI https://app.derive.xyz) and https://testnet.api.derive.xyz/v3 (testnet, UI https://testnet.app.derive.xyz), and say the separate 'Derive Wallet' was removed (the owner is now your own EOA or multisig). CCXT added v3 support in 4.5.88 (master derive.py uses api.derive.xyz/v3 and testnet.api.derive.xyz/v3; latest on PyPI is 4.5.90). LumiBot's setup.py only requires ccxt>=4.5.50, so a page written now would describe a setup that cannot connect on the pinned/installed CCXT. Also, v3 CCXT needs a subaccount_id option (and a deriveWalletAddress option when the privateKey is a session key for another owner wallet), which the plain <ID>_PRIVATE_KEY / <ID>_WALLET_ADDRESS env vars do not set. Facts gathered for a later page: trading uses session keys, delegated signing keys created with private/set_session_key (or in the UI) that carry protocol scopes such as trade:orderbook:all and an expiry and subaccount list; a key with no protocol scopes is read-only; only the owner or admin can withdraw or transfer to any recipient, so a trade-only session key cannot (https://docs.derive.xyz/authentication/session-keys, https://docs.derive.xyz/authentication/access-scopes). The first deposit (on Ethereum L1) creates the account and its first subaccount (https://docs.derive.xyz/getting-started/quickstart). Revisit after LumiBot requires ccxt>=4.5.88, then rerun facts generation and market discovery.
